Aunt Wang sighed faintly and said behind my back, "Go on then. It's just a pity for that child; it didn't even get to take a single look at this world..."

***

Battling the wind and snow, I walked to the village chief's front gate. Even before entering the house, I could already feel the heat of the underfloor heating rushing toward my face.

They always said the village chief's family was wealthy. Ordinary people like us could only install radiator panels, and even in the coldest weather, the temperature wouldn't go up.

Only the multi-story house of the village chief had underfloor heating installed on every single floor, with the decoration costs alone totaling nearly fifty thousand yuan.

Yet now that I knew how that money had been made, even the floor heating felt a bit scorching to my feet.

The village chief was sitting on the threshold, smoking with an air of defeat. His bald head, which barely had any hair to begin with, was almost plucked clean by his own hands.

Raising his head to see me, his tone was laced with utter exhaustion. "Xiaolu's here. Your grandmother is inside."

After changing into slippers and stepping inside, I heard Liu Yazhi's faint, sobbing whimpers.

The bedroom door wasn't closed, and I saw Liu Yazhi sitting propped up against the head of the bed, holding a swaddle in her arms. That must have been the stillborn baby...

The village chief's wife, Aunt Tian, couldn't help but angrily curse, "Cry, cry, cry! All you know how to do is cry! Can't you see there are guests in the house? It's the New Year, who wants to listen to you mourning!

Married for five years, and even a hen knows how to hatch several clutches of eggs, yet you can't drop a single one! You finally managed to get pregnant, only to give birth to this sort of abomination...

Let me tell you, hurry up and throw it as far away as you can; I don't want to see it ever again!"

Everyone in the village knew that Aunt Tian and Liu Yazhi had a very poor mother-in-law and daughter-in-law relationship.

Back when Liu Yazhi married Tian Hongwei, Tian Hongwei was only the lowest-ranking employee at the housing bureau.

Later, when Tian Hongwei made it big, Aunt Tian felt that Liu Yazhi, who only had a junior high school education, wasn't good enough for her son.

Tian Hongwei got involved with other women outside, and the frequency of his home visits gradually decreased.

Aunt Tian believed this was entirely Liu Yazhi's fault; she couldn't even manage her own man, causing her to miss out on seeing her son and holding her grandson, and she gave Liu Yazhi harsh looks day in and day out.

Feeling unsettled and thinking Aunt Tian's words were far too harsh, I couldn't help but speak up.

"Auntie, Sister Yazhi is a human being, not a laying hen; she has the right to choose whether to give birth or not! Which law states that a married woman must bear children to continue a man's lineage?

Besides, ever since Sister Yazhi got pregnant, your son hasn't come back to check on her even once, right? As the father, he hasn't fulfilled a single bit of responsibility or obligation, and now that something has gone wrong with the baby, why are you only scolding Sister Yazhi instead of your precious son?"

Aunt Tian lost face from being rebuked by me, so she flipped the curtain aside and walked out. "I have nothing to say to you uneducated brats!"

Liu Yazhi cast a grateful look in my direction. "Thank you, Xiaolu."

Seeing that her eyes were swollen from crying, I wanted to step forward and offer a few words of comfort, but my peripheral vision caught the swaddle she was holding in her arms, which gave me a genuine fright...

That stillborn infant was blue and purple all over, and its skin was actually covered in transparent scales, layer upon overlapping layer, looking frighteningly like a black fish pulled from a river.

Was... was this even human?

Could it be that the village chief's family really incurred divine retribution, which was why Liu Yazhi gave birth to such a deformed creature?

The sight gave me goosebumps all over, and I involuntarily took two steps back.

Guessing that I would have this reaction, Liu Yazhi glanced at me indifferently, gently rocking the stillborn infant in her arms as if coaxing it to sleep.

"Terrifying, right? I was scared too when I first saw it. But after all, it's flesh of my flesh; no matter what it grows up to look like, I won't despise it."

As she spoke, tears fell again, and she choked out, "Actually, I knew about all the things Hongwei did, but I couldn't stop him. I guessed that sooner or later he would face retribution, but why did Heaven have to take it out on my child? It's innocent!"

Having never given birth to a child nor experienced maternal love, I couldn't truly empathize and could only offer persuasion. "You're so young, you'll have more children in the future. But since you've already seen through Tian Hongwei, you'd better cut ties sooner rather than later."

Liu Yazhi gave a sarcastic smile and said coldly, "It's not that simple. He made me the laughingstock of the entire village for five years, made me unable to hold my head high in front of my own family, and even killed my child! Now he wants to brush me off with a single divorce certificate, there's no such cheap deal..."

Seeing that she was somewhat consumed by her obsession, I didn't dare say anything more and left the bedroom to look for Granny.

Granny was sitting on a chair in the backyard, her expression looking helpless and exhausted, her face cast in an ashen gray hue.

Her withered, branch-like hands hung at her sides, dried blood still staining the gaps between her fingers, and her chapped lips moved slightly. "The deities refuse to help me... I made a mistake, and the deities refuse to help me anymore..."

I walked up to her and softly called out, "Granny."

Granny raised her head. Those pale eyes were brimming with tears as she took my hand and said, "Xiaolu, the deities won't help me! I can feel the divine power in my body fading away bit by bit. Perhaps my time is almost up..."

My heart clenched violently. "Granny, don't scare me!"

Hearing my voice, Granny calmed down instead. "Granny isn't scaring you. Granny is already over seventy years old; by any calculation, my time has come. There's nothing to be afraid of.

It's just that you haven't crossed this tribulation yet, and Granny can't let it go. If I leave now, no one will be left to protect our Xiaolu..."

The bridge of my nose stung, and I almost burst into tears.

Granny had once said that when a shaman was approaching death, the deities would gradually withdraw their power from her body, turning her back into an ordinary person.

If a shaman felt increasingly powerless while casting spells, it meant their time limit was near.

This process was called divine withdrawal.

Could it be that because Granny defied the heavens to alter my fate and angered the deities, they were no longer willing to help her?

My heart was filled with guilt and distress, yet unable to do anything, I could only comfort her. "Granny, stop saying such things. Let's go home. It's almost noon, and I'll cook something delicious for you when we get back."

Granny nodded and stood up with my support, walking outside.

Passing by the village chief, she said in a hoarse voice, "That child must be dealt with as soon as possible, sink it into the river. It cannot be buried."

The village chief didn't ask further and nodded with a heavy expression.

Back home, I took the pork liver out of the cellar, thinking that Granny must be exhausted from staying up all night, so I boiled a red date and pork liver soup for her to nourish her *qi* and blood.

Granny remained completely silent from the moment she entered the house. The two of us ate this meal in silence and then returned to our respective rooms to rest.

Lying on the bed, tossing and turning while thinking of Granny's words, I secretly wiped away the tears at the corners of my eyes with the quilt.

Perhaps because I had shed too many tears, I drifted into a hazy sleep...

Amidst the blur, I felt a cool hand gently caressing my cheek.

Opening my eyes, a man as slender and flawless as jade appeared in my line of sight.

chapters.title: Big Forest Timber
chapters.content:
Half of a cold, white wristbone was exposed from his wide cuff, and his fingertips traced repeatedly along the contour of my face.

I instinctively shrank back into the corner, seeing him lying lazily on my side, a casual expression hiding a trace of mockery, as if he were studying me closely.

Long Mingyuan?

Didn’t he say he would never see me again in the future? Why did he come back tonight!

Going back on his word...

"Why is it you again!" I asked, puzzled.

"Again?" Long Mingyuan raised an eyebrow, his thin lips curving slightly upward. "I've come to find my princess consort, is there something wrong with that?"

"Who is your princess consort!" I felt my scalp tingle and my whole body grow cold at this ambiguous title.

"I am the Dragon King of this river, and you are my chosen princess consort. We are going to be wed and married very soon. Aren't you happy?" His tone was too frivolous, yet those azure eyes held no trace of a smile.

Happy, my foot!

When did I ever agree to marry you!

"Didn't you promise me that you would never appear in my dreams again! I don't want to be any Dragon King's consort, you should go find someone else as soon as possible!" I was on the verge of a breakdown, jumping off the bed and running toward the door.

"Did I give you permission to leave?"

The voice of the person behind me suddenly turned fierce and cold. With a slight lift of his right hand, I was actually pulled back by a powerful suction force.

"Ugh..." My back slammed hard against the unyielding brick kang, hurting me enough to let out a muffled groan.

Long Mingyuan's supremely handsome face gradually enlarged in my pupils. The corners of his lips curved into a teasing smile. "Be a good girl, Xiaolu, come let me give you a hug!"

I felt something was a bit off...

The person in front of me looked and was dressed exactly like Long Mingyuan, but his brows and eyes faintly exuded a sinister aura. He was a completely different person from the aloof and exquisite man of last night.

How could there be two Long Mingyuans?

'Long Mingyuan' controlled my body, leaving me unable to move.

At this moment, he was extremely close to me, the breath he exhaled spraying against my forehead and blowing my wispy bangs around. Yet, I couldn't smell the faint hint of ambergris from last night.

Those icy blue eyes stared fixedly at me. "Hmm... how come I feel like you've gotten uglier compared to before?"

Damn it, is that any way to talk!

"Never mind, it doesn't matter, as long as it's you... My princess consort, hurry over to the Dragon King Temple at the entrance of the village to find me. I can't wait to consummate our marriage with you!"

This speech was dripping with ambiguity, but the wicked arc at the corner of his mouth betrayed him.

My thoughts were completely confused by him. Frowning, I said, "Didn't you tell me to stay away from the Dragon King Temple at the village entrance and that I must never go there?"

'Long Mingyuan's' expression shifted slightly, and he gave a cold laugh. " Oh? When did I ever say such a thing? You must have remembered wrong!"

Just as I was wondering if this Long Mingyuan had a split personality, the light in the outhouse belonging to Aunt Wang across the door suddenly turned on.

By the dim light, I clearly saw the appearance of the man in front of me.

The cinnabar mole between his brows, vibrant and red like bleeding sap, was gone...

I was deeply shocked and shouted loudly, "You are not Long Mingyuan!"

The man's expression instantly turned playful. He arched his eyebrow, tilted his head, and said, "You found out!"

"Who on earth are you?" My back was pressed flat against the wall, yet I was still curling inward desperately.

He hooked the corner of his lips and transformed back into his true appearance.

The dark-colored long robe on his body turned into a white garment. His facial features were extremely similar to Long Mingyuan's, but the angles of his jaw were slightly greener and more youthful. He possessed a bit more wickedness and a bit less profundity than Long Mingyuan.

Only his eyes were completely inconsistent with Long Mingyuan's; they were as cold, clear, and limpid as Heavenly Mountain jasper, holding an imperceptible, dark sarcasm.

"I have already answered this question. I am the Dragon King of this Heilongjiang River, Long Mingze!"

I tentatively asked, "Then what is your relationship with Long Mingyuan?"

Long Mingze half-leaned against my pillow and said idly, "No relation."

How could there be two people in this world with such similar appearances?

Unless...

"Oh, I get it! Long Mingyuan is your twin brother?" I suddenly understood.

Sure enough, upon hearing this title, a layer of chill swept across Long Mingze's green pupils. He gave a light sneer, "That impostor is not even worthy of being called my brother! Also, why do you always bring him up in front of me? How a-pissing-off!"

It seemed his relationship with his brother was not good...

I looked at him suspiciously. "You say you are the Dragon King of this river?"

Long Mingze proudly lifted his chin. "That's right."

"How can you prove it?" I asked expressionlessly.

Long Mingze choked for a moment, narrowing his slender eyes, his tone somewhat displeased. "Have you never heard of the origin of this river?"

Feigning ignorance, I shook my head.

He explained impatiently, "A thousand years ago, in order to save the common people, I fought a life-and-death battle with the black flood dragon Long Mingyuan. I suffered extremely heavy injuries, and my soul was nearly scattered.

To save me, the villagers built a dragon-suppressing coffin, letting me recuperate in the coffin for a thousand years, until recently when there were signs of my awakening.

However, I have now lost all my spiritual power and cannot restore my true form, so I can only visit you through dreams."

His words subverted all my previous guesses.

Long Mingze was the little white dragon who exhausted his spiritual power to save all living beings, while Long Mingyuan turned out to be the black flood dragon that I had sealed away with my blood in a past life!

This sounded pretty much consistent with the versions passed down by word of mouth among the old folks in the village.

But I remembered my grandmother saying that rumors should not be entirely believed...

The feeling this Long Mingze gave me was very bad. His entire body exuded an evil and sinister aura reminiscent of hell, making one's blood run cold.

"......Lord Dragon King, did you also eat those young boys and girls?" I asked cautiously.

Long Mingze licked his thin lower lip, tilting his head with interest to look at me sideways. "What do you think?"

I wished I could turn into an earthworm and burrow into a crack in the ground; what was there left to think!

"Rest assured, I never eat people." Sensing the vigilance in my eyes, he said with a half-smile, "Since you repeatedly mention Long Mingyuan, you must have already seen that impostor brother of mine. He is about to break the seal, and the day he makes a comeback, the mortal world will be plunged into devastation..."

The corners of my mouth twitched slightly, feeling as though I were listening to a fairy tale.

"I am currently still in a dormant state. I need you to come to the Dragon King Temple to awaken me and help me recover my spiritual power."

Long Mingze's tone was extremely arrogant and proud. "Now that the gods have fallen, only I can defeat him!"

I was half-skeptical of his words. "Then how can I awaken you?"

Like a prince waking Sleeping Beauty, by giving him a kiss...

His thin lips moved slightly, and he dragged out his tone, "Marry me to ward off bad luck."

What the hell...

Isn't warding off bad luck through marriage an ancient folk custom?

Having an able-bodied woman marry a sickly man to counteract bad luck with joyous events, hoping to achieve a healing effect.

Does the dignified Lord Dragon King actually need to...

chapters.title: Roadside Soil
chapters.content:
"Lord Dragon King, since ancient times, weddings and funerals require a proper matchmaker and the command of parents! We must do things by the rules, right? If you really want to marry me, you must first ask my grandmother's opinion..."

I smiled apologetically and declined.

I thought to herself that Granny would never agree to me marrying the Dragon King; she should have a way to help me escape this calamity.

If I were forced to marry the Dragon King, I'd rather be a spinster for the rest of my life...

Instead, Long Mingze gave a cold sneer. "As early as twenty years ago, I already went to propose marriage! Your betrothal gifts have also been received by them. Once you come to the Dragon King Temple, we can enter the bridal chamber!"

"What?" I was shocked. "You must be mistaken. Twenty years ago, I wasn't even born yet. Who on earth did you give the betrothal gifts to?"

Long Mingze evaded the question. "In short, our marriage pact has long been set in stone, and you have no say in the matter!"

With that, he winked at me, deliberately pressing close to the tip of my nose with ambiguity. "My princess consort, do not be deceived by Long Mingyuan any longer. I am waiting for you at the Dragon King Temple at the village entrance. I hope you won't make me wait too long!"

Having said that, his outline gradually faded into the night...

***

The next day, I woke up from bed to find that a blizzard had been raging all night outside.

The snow piled up in the courtyard had once again surpassed my ankles. Fearing that Granny might slip and fall, I quickly put on my padded jacket and went out to sweep the snow.

Wielding the broom in my hand, I recalled the dream from the night before.

Great, now I indeed don't have erotic dreams anymore, I've upgraded to dreaming of the Haier Brothers!

First, I dreamed of someone named Long Mingyuan, and then I dreamed of someone named Long Mingze.

Not only did the two brothers look identical, but they also insisted on crossing each other.

One told me never to go to the Dragon King Temple at the village entrance, while the other said he was waiting for me inside the Dragon King Temple.

One wanted my life, while the other wanted me to marry him to ward off bad luck?

No... one of them must be lying!

Who on earth was trying to harm me?

Or were both of them trying to harm me?

The information I had right now was still too scarce to make a detailed judgment, so I could only classify both of them as suspects.

Apart from Granny, I trusted no one!

Yet in my heart, I actually leaned more toward Long Mingyuan, because his words were consistent with Granny's, and Granny surely wouldn't lie to me!

Moreover, Long Mingyuan gave me a sense of familiarity, as if we had met before. I could be certain that he was the man who came to my dreams every night to dally with me.

Perhaps because of the high frequency of our 'deep communication', seeing him appear before me made me feel at ease.

However, when Long Mingze approached me, the sinister aura radiating from him terrified me, making me want to flee uncontrollably.

I should go ask Granny; she must know who the real Dragon King is!

At that moment, another knock came from outside the door...

"Knock, knock, knock..."

Having already developed a conditioned reflex, the moment I heard a knock on the door, I wanted to dive back into my room.

But in broad daylight, even if there were ghosts, they wouldn't dare come out during the morning when the Yang energy was at its peak, right?

Besides, didn't Long Mingyuan say he had sent Zhang Dezhu off to be reincarnated?

Clutching the broom, I walked on tiptoe toward the large iron gate and peered through the crack, only to see a middle-aged man and woman I had never seen before standing outside my house.

The man looked to be around forty-seven or forty-eight, wearing a black overcoat with his hair slicked back and a leather bag tucked under his arm.

The woman wore a purple mink fur coat, with a crystal-clear jade pendant hanging from her neck. She was well-maintained and looked to be just a little over forty.

Everything about them gave off the vibe of sudden wealth, but why would such a wealthy family brave the heavy snow to come out to our place?

Were they looking for Granny again?

Cautiously, I opened the gate and asked, "Can I help you?"

To my surprise, upon seeing me, the middle-aged couple froze slightly before the woman suddenly pulled me into her arms, weeping mournfully, "Oh, mother's heart and soul, we've finally found you!"

The pungent smell of perfume on the woman almost choked me unconscious. Without even trying to process what she was shouting, I forcefully struggled out of her thick mink fur.

"Who on earth are you? Speak properly, keep your hands to yourself!"

The middle-aged couple exchanged glances, and the man stepped forward, a deliberately ingratiating smile plastered on his face. "Little girl, you are twenty years old by lunar reckoning, and your name is Xiaolu, right?"

Hesitantly, I nodded.

"You've had no father or mother since you were little, and your grandmother picked you up from the woods, right?" the woman asked again.

A vague sense of foreboding rose in my heart, and I bit my lower lip, refusing to answer.

At that moment, Granny walked out from her room. Without a second word, she picked up her walking stick and drove the people away. "Who let you come here! Get the hell out of my house right now, Xiaolu is not going anywhere with you!"

The man took the full force of Granny's walking stick, gritting his teeth against the pain as he said, "Granny Lin, I know you harbor resentment toward us. It was wrong of us to abandon Xiaoluo back then, but Xiaoluo is our biological daughter after all. You can't keep me from seeing her!"

It felt as though something had violently collapsed in my mind, my ears buzzing as I looked at Granny in disbelief.

"Granny, didn't you say I was an orphan whose parents died long ago?"

Granny's expression was grim, her pale, blank pupils looking exceptionally eerie. "Parents like these, how are they any different from the dead!"

The woman covered her face and began to cry. "Granny Lin, we had no choice either! Back then during the Northeast layoffs, both the child's father and I were laid off. Our family was so poor we didn't even have rice; we simply couldn't afford to raise Xiaoluo.

We had no choice but to leave her in the woods, thinking that perhaps a kind-hearted person would pass by and save her. Even if she just got a sip of rice water, it would still be better than suffering along with us!"

Granny slammed her walking stick heavily onto the ground, shouting with furious, tearful rage, "Bah! It was so freezing that winter, and you abandoned a month-old baby in the woods. If the Deer Deity hadn't brought her to me, she would have long since been eaten by a black bear. You two must have deliberately wanted her dead!"

The woman's expression froze as she offered a weak defense, "No... we didn't!"

Hearing this, I understood in my heart. So I wasn't an orphan without father or mother!

I had a father and a mother, yet they abandoned me the moment I was born and threw me into the woods...

Even a tiger won't eat its own cubs; how could their hearts be so cruel!

I walked up to them, stiffened my neck, and asked, "Are you really my biological parents?"

The man nodded eagerly. "Yes, Xiaoluo, we even brought your birth certificate, take a look..."

I took the yellowed piece of paper handed over by the man, which bore the words "Medical Birth Certificate" printed in black on a green background.

The birth date recorded on it matched mine precisely, and the lower right corner bore the red stamp of our township hospital.

"Wen Wan..." I murmured, reading out the name written in the name column.

Wiping the tears from the corners of her eyes, the woman said softly, "Yes, your father's surname is Wen, and we named you Wen Wan. Xiaoluo, you've grown up so much, and you've turned out so pretty..."

With that, she reached out her hand to touch my face.

However, I ruthlessly slapped her hand away. "Don't touch me!"

chapters.title: Sword-Point Gold
chapters.content:
The woman stood frozen in place, staring at me in disbelief, a trace of complexity mixed in her eyes.

"You're from the Yelong Village across the river, aren't you?" I asked coldly, demanding an explanation.

Our mountainous region was divided into south and north of the river. Those living on the south bank of the Heilongjiang River were called Dragon-Guarding Village, and those on the north bank were called Yelong Village.

Usually, there was very little interaction between the two villages. Though drinking from the same river, they treated each other like strangers.

The south said the people in the north were eccentric and calculating.

The south said the people in the north were poor, so poor they couldn't even afford eight dishes for Chinese New Year. They mutually looked down on each other.

The reason I concluded they were from Yelong Village across the river was because it was currently snowing heavily, and the roads into the mountains were already blocked.

If they had been cruel enough to abandon me in the woods back then, they certainly wouldn't brave a blizzard and walk into the mountains just to find a child lost for nearly twenty years.

But if they lived in Yelong Village, once the river froze over, walking across the ice took only fifteen minutes.

The middle-aged man and woman nodded.

Seeing them admit it, the tears I had suppressed in my heart suddenly rushed out of my eyes.

My biological parents hadn't died; they were alive and well, living in a village just a few kilometers away from me.

For the past twenty years, they had countless opportunities to acknowledge me, yet they kept delaying and refused to come find me!

And they still claimed they didn't abandon me!

If that was the case, why come looking for me now?

"Speak. What on earth are you thinking?" I raised my hand to wipe the tear tracks from my face, my tone devoid of any emotion.

Seeing my attitude so cold, the woman covered her face and began to cry again.

The man sighed, "Let me explain, Xiaowan. It was your mother and I who wronged you in this matter..."

As the man narrated in a gentle, continuous stream, I learned that they were originally from the south. The man was named Wen Youcai, and the woman was Fu Hongmei.

Earlier in life, following the older members of their family, they had ventured north to Manchuria (Chuang Guandong) and ended up working at the Greater Khingan Mountains Forestry Administration. But after working there for barely two years, they encountered the Northeast China state-owned enterprise layoffs (Xiagang) wave.

Because Wen Youcai and Fu Hongmei had non-local household registrations, they bore the brunt of it and became the first batch of laid-off workers.

"When your mother and I were laid off, she had just conceived you, and our family was so poor we couldn't even afford rice gruel. We adults could go hungry, but you were so small, how could we bear to let you suffer this hardship with us..."

I interrupted him with complete indifference, "Is this why you abandoned me? No way. Even if the family was too poor to even light the stove, I hadn't been weaned yet. Surely we weren't out of breast milk?"

The woman sniffled and choked out, "We didn't abandon you because of that... It was because one night you suddenly had severe convulsions, difficulty breathing, and your whole little face turned purple with asphyxiation. We carried you to the town to see a doctor and spent our few remaining savings.

The doctor said you had congenital asthma, a 'wealthy disease' that couldn't tolerate cold or heat and required staying away from allergens, otherwise there was a risk of relapse.

The doctor asked us at the time if we planned on long-term treatment. We wanted to treat you, but we had no money!"

"So, you threw me into the woods?" I clenched my fists, an irrepressible anger surging in my heart, and said angrily.

"...Later on, we found out you were taken in by Granny Lin, and we felt relieved. They always said a witch doctor is also a doctor; perhaps she could cure your illness...

Xiaowan, don't blame your mom and dad. We had no choice!

You must have heard of the Northeast layoff wave, right? Back then, the streets were full of beggars and blood-sellers, and many women went to singing and dancing halls to sell their bodies to support their families, or went to Guangdong to become foot-massage girls.

If we could have afforded the treatment for this illness, we wouldn't have thrown our own biological daughter out!" Wen Youcai said with deep grief and remorse.

I bit my teeth tightly, my heart hurting as if it were being torn apart.

Mother or not, Liu Yazhi could hold such a terrifying monster of a child in her arms, unable to bear burying it.

Yet my biological parents threw me into the woods to fend for myself simply because treating my illness cost money!

I felt only bitterness and resentment toward them, unable to muster even a sliver of affection.

If Wen Youcai hadn't mentioned today that I had congenital asthma, I truly wouldn't have known I had ever suffered from such a disease.

From as far back as I could remember, I had run wild in the mountains with the neighborhood children without showing any symptoms.

Thinking about it now, Granny must have cured me.

She not only saved my life, she also cured my illness...

"Xiaowan, come back with Mom and Dad! Your mom and dad have made a lot of money doing business these past two years, and our family has built a three-story small Western-style house now. The conditions are much better than your grandmother's place here. Come back with us, and Mom and Dad will do our best to make it up to you." With that, Fu Hongmei reached her hand out toward me.

I stepped back to avoid it and asked aloud, "Since you knew long ago that Granny took me in, why haven't you come to see me once in these twenty years? Why do you only now remember to pick me up and take me home?"

Their eyes flickered evasively, and they faltered, "Xiaowan, it's not that we didn't want to take you back; it's that Granny Lin wouldn't let us near you...

She believed that since we abandoned you in the first place, we had no qualification to ask for you back.

Your mother and I came three or four times, and each time your grandmother drove us out with her walking stick!

She even said if we came again, she'd fight us to the death with a knife..."

Hearing this, I turned around to look at Granny. She was standing behind the herbal medicine rack in the courtyard, wearing a long black padded coat. The whole person looked gloomy, so solitary, and so stubborn.

The villagers all said my grandmother had a rather bad temper. Coupled with the fact that she was a spirit-catching shaman, and people always harbor fear of the unknown, they rarely interacted with her on regular days, only coming to find her when something happened.

Especially the children; they all thought Granny's pale pupils were terrifying and hid far away when they saw her.

Yet I knew Granny possessed the most merciful heart in the world, which was why she treated me like her own biological granddaughter, using the money earned from selling herbs to put me through school and university.

Granny didn't let Wen Youcai and the others come looking for me because she was afraid it would disrupt my peaceful life now.

And Granny's misgivings were not wrong. Wen Youcai and the others could abandon me once, and they could abandon me a second time. How could she bear to let me suffer such pain again?

"Then what are you coming to find me for now? Is one of you on your deathbed and need me to smash the mourning basin or cry at your grave?" I mocked mercilessly.

"Xiaowan, your grandmother is advanced in age and can no longer take care of you. But Mom and Dad are still young and can support you through university, and later send you abroad for graduate school.

Just come back with us! That way, your grandmother can also enjoy a few years of peace and comfort.

Anyway, we live right across the river; whenever you miss her, you can come over to see her anytime!" Wen Youcai didn't give up, still trying to persuade me with nice words.

I turned back to look at Granny in the corner. Aside from her initial emotional agitation, she had remained completely silent from beginning to end, quietly watching us with those pale, ghostly pupils.

Only I could read the lingering attachment and reluctance to part within those terrifying eyes...

***

chapters.title: Mountain Head Fire
chapters.content:
Seeing this, Wen Youcai took a thick stack of red banknotes from his bag and handed them toward Granny.

"Granny Lin, thank you for troubling yourself to take care of our Xiaowan all these years. This money is for you to spend during the New Year. Please accept it!"

Granny turned aside, refusing to accept the money, and said harshly, "Take your stinking money and get lost!"

A fleeting flash of ruthlessness crossed Wen Youcai's face before he instantly concealed it, smiling ingratiatingly, "Granny Lin, even if you don't think of yourself, you have to think of the child!

Xiaowan is already twenty years old, and the down jacket she's wearing is still a style from several years ago. She'll be laughed at by her classmates when she goes to a big city!

If she comes back with us, our home has everything she could want. She won't have to cut firewood and boil water every day to live a hard life anymore!"

Granny's chapped lips trembled slightly, unable to speak for a long time.

I guessed Granny must have thought about how her days were numbered and truly felt she couldn't take care of me anymore.

She had helped many people throughout her life without accepting a single cent, leaving her household as barren as washed walls. Even if she were really gone one day, the only thing left for me would be this half-collapsed, dilapidated farmhouse.

Yet precisely because Granny was advanced in age, I had to stay by her side. She raised me when I was small, so I had to tend to her when she was old to repay this debt of gratitude.

As for Wen Youcai and Fu Hongmei, they had abandoned me long ago. Legally and emotionally, they had nothing to do with me anymore!

I gritted my teeth, picked up the broom that had fallen on the ground, and drove the two of them out the door. "Hurry up and leave! I don't want to see you ever again! Don't come to Granny's and my home again in the future. I am never going back with you!"

"Xiaowan, are you disowning your mom and dad?" The woman covered her mouth and sobbed.

"Don't call me Xiaowan anymore!" I shouted coldly, "Listen well: my name is Lin Jianlu, and I am Granny Lin's biological granddaughter! Don't ever come to disturb Granny's and my life again, or I'll beat you once every time I see you!"

With that, I locked the front gate right in front of them.

Wen Youcai and Fu Hongmei were still shouting outside the door, "Xiaowan, open the door! You can't just disown your mom and dad!"

I leaned against the large iron gate, feeling as though all the strength had been drained from my body. Unable to support myself any longer, I slowly slumped down into the snow.

In just a single day, I had gained parents, only to lose them again...

Granny came to my side and let out a long sigh, "The ground is cold, get up quickly."

I took hold of Granny's icy hand, sniffing as I said, "Granny, let's go back inside."

Granny said nothing more, and I supported her as we returned indoors.

Outside, heavy snow was flying. I closed the door and began making lunch, preparing a large pot of pickled cabbage stewed with blood sausage, and stir-frying a plate of Earth Three-Fresh (potatoes, eggplant, and green peppers).

While eating, I couldn't help glancing out the window, only to find that Wen Youcai and Fu Hongmei were still sitting right at our doorstep, their noses and cheeks flushed red from the cold, sniffing as they looked inside.

They must have smelled the aroma of my cooking and were starving.

Of course, I wasn't going to send food out to them. Given their selfish and self-serving nature, they would probably run off by themselves after another two hours of hunger.

As it turned out, I had underestimated them!

When dinnertime arrived, I raised my head for a quick glance and found they were still sitting on the steps of our house.

The clothes on their bodies had been covered in white by the heavy snow, with frost coating their eyelashes and the tips of their hair. From a distance, they looked like two snowmen.

If they were going to be this tenacious and persistent, why didn't they do it earlier!

I angrily poked the rice in my bowl with my chopsticks until Granny scolded me, "Don't waste food!"

She closed her eyes, picked up a piece of meat with her chopsticks, placed it in my bowl, and said meaningfully, "Soft-hearted already? If you can't bear to watch, just go back with them!"

I looked at the piece of meat in my bowl and shook my head. "I'm not soft-hearted. When they threw me into the woods back then, they didn't care if I was cold or hungry either. Who are they putting on this pitiful act for now?"

Granny snorted disdainfully. "Good thing you know! If you can't bear it, just don't look. Once they freeze enough to not take it anymore, they'll leave on their own."

Hearing Granny's words, I stopped looking toward the window.

Before going to sleep, I made a point of pulling the curtains shut tightly, leaving not even a sliver of a gap.

Out of sight, out of mind. They could stand guard all they liked; in any case, I would never abandon Granny!

Just as I was about to take out that unread university physics textbook to lull myself to sleep, I suddenly heard Aunt Wang across the street cry out in alarm, "Oh my! Why are there two living people lying at this doorway? Old man, come out and take a look!"

I hesitated for three seconds, then threw on my down jacket and ran out.

After all, if anything happened to these two people right at our doorstep, Granny and I would still be the targets of gossip in the village. I didn't want Granny, who had lived a righteous and upright life, to bear the reproach of refusing to render aid in her later years!

I opened the gate, and Aunt Wang's husband had already brought the Wen Youcai couple into their home to warm up.

Seeing me, Aunt Wang pulled me into the room. "Xiaolu, what's going on here? I just went out to dump the trash and saw two extra things at your doorstep. I was wondering when your family got stone lions as guardian beasts, and when I walked closer, they turned out to be two living people!"

Seeing Aunt Wang's husband feeding hot water to the two people lying on the kang (heated brick bed), I recounted the whole story with reddened eyes.

After hearing it, Aunt Wang sighed with emotion. "Xiaolu, I can understand how you feel, and I agree with you staying to take care of Granny Lin. But after all, they are your biological parents. Even if you don't go with them, you can't just watch them freeze to death outside!"

I bit my lip in silence, unable to think of a good solution for the moment.

Aunt Wang put an arm around my shoulders and advised earnestly, "Xiaolu, the world isn't just black and white. Even if you can't be family, it doesn't mean you have to be enemies! How about this? Once they wake up, I'll help persuade them to go back first."

I nodded and looked at her gratefully. "Thank you, Aunt Wang, for causing you trouble."

"Good child, hurry back and get some sleep," Aunt Wang walked me out the door.

When I got home, passing by Granny's bedroom, I noticed she was sleeping very deeply and hadn't been awakened by Aunt Wang's shouts.

This made me feel uneasy and anxious. It seemed that ever since Granny returned from the village chief's house, her sleeping time had been growing longer day by day.

I searched online, and some people said it was a mental issue, while others suggested it was more likely a cerebrovascular disease.

Now the mountains were sealed by heavy snow, and the road out of the village was still blocked.

Once spring arrived, I would definitely have to take Granny to the provincial hospital for a comprehensive checkup.

I lay back down under the covers and fell asleep shortly after.

In my dream, I saw Long Mingze again.

He was dressed in white purer than snow, his silver hair fluttering like an immortal's. He stood by the bed, looking down to scrutinize me, a playful smile lingering on his wicked yet handsome face.

"My consort, why haven't you come to the Dragon King's Temple to find me yet? Could it be that you heard we were going to consummate our marriage and got shy?"

chapters.title: River Water
chapters.content:
Feeling depressed and in a foul mood, I didn't bother to address his teasing tone and brushed him off. "Lord Dragon King, I am not going to the Dragon King Temple at the village entrance, nor do I want to have anything to do with you dragons and river serpents.

Take your betrothal gifts back to whoever accepted them. Anyway, I didn't take a single cent, so leave me alone!"

The sneer at the corners of Long Mingze's lips gradually vanished, replaced by a terrifying, sinister gloom.

His long fingers hooked under my chin, his voice cold and cruel. "Lin Jianlu, you think far too highly of yourself! Do you really think I'm that eager to marry you? If you weren't the only one capable of waking me, I wouldn't even deign to look at you twice!"

My chin throbbed with pain from his grip. Helpless and unable to move, I glared viciously at him and retorted, "You think little of me? Well, I think even less of you! Since we can't stand the sight of each other, wouldn't it be just perfect to call off this engagement?"

Long Mingze narrowed his jade-green eyes, which blazed with fury. "You actually look down on me... What right do you have to look down on me?! Who is it that you fancy instead, Long Mingyuan?"

I stubbornly fired back, "At least Long Mingyuan doesn't go around abducting innocent maidens by force!"

The moment the words left my mouth, I suddenly remembered that Long Mingyuan indeed hadn't abducted me in broad daylight; he had simply broken into my dreams and forced himself upon me...

These two brothers really were cut from the same cloth; not a single one of them was any good!

Hearing this, Long Mingze let out a sound as if he had heard something immensely amusing. His handsome face, cast in shadow, was indistinct.

Yet I could sense he was smiling, and his smile was deeply unsettling.

In an extremely soft tone, he uttered a sentence I couldn't quite understand: "Since that's the case, I'll grant you your wish..."

"What?" I asked, baffled.

In a flash, his expression reverted to one of ruthless ferocity. He sneered, "The bond between you and me was sealed long ago. In this life, you are my person alive, and my ghost in death! Even if you flee to the ends of the earth, I will drag you back. Don't even dream of shaking me off!"

I was so angry I couldn't utter a single word, staring at him with a gaze full of despair and resentment.

Long Mingze flicked his sleeve and withdrew his hand, profound contempt hidden deep in his eyes. He muttered under his breath, "With a flat figure like yours, no hips, no chest, I honestly haven't the faintest idea what Long Mingyuan ever saw in you..."

"I am absolutely not going to the Dragon King Temple, no matter what you say!" I rolled my eyes at him, exasperated.

Who didn't know how to hurl insults? I desperately wanted to retort that his white hair and green eyes made him look like a second-year middle schooler obsessed with cosplay!

"Are you certain you won't go?" Long Mingze's voice rose at the end, laced with mockery.

"Not going."

Granny told me not to go, so I wouldn't go!

"Lin Jianlu, a thousand years have passed, and your temper is still as stubborn as ever. Truly annoying!" Long Mingze gave a cold scoff, pressed his palm downward, and slammed it onto my forehead.

Just as I was about to curse him with a *'You're even more annoying!'*...

I suddenly found my body seized and manipulated like a marionette, forced to stand up. Out of my control, I pushed open the bedroom door, my limbs stiff as a walking corpse as I shuffled out toward the courtyard.

The biting winter wind was piercingly cold, and clad only in my thin pajamas, I was chilled through to the bone in an instant.

My legs crossed the high doorsill of their own accord, swaying and stumbling down the village path leading toward the riverbank.

If anyone happened to be up in the middle of the night, they would undoubtedly have been terrified by my disheveled, wild-haired appearance.

Yet I had no control over my body whatsoever; my consciousness was razor-sharp, but my physical form refused to obey.

What on earth did Long Mingze do to me?

"Since you refused to be obedient, I had no choice but to use a bit of dream-control magic to make you come looking for me at the Dragon King Temple of your own accord!" Long Mingze seemed capable of hearing my inner thoughts, his voice ringing in my ears with a wicked, seductive smile.

Using my subconscious mind, I told him, "Let me go! I don't want to go to the Dragon King Temple!"

"No, you do," his voice sounded entirely apathetic.

I, "..."

The freezing northern wind was on the verge of turning the blood in my veins to ice. If this continued, I feared I would be frozen to death out here in the open.

Abruptly, a patch of withered reeds appeared ahead, and not far away, the icy river surface reflected a silvery-gray glow under the moonlight.

Alarm bells clanged fiercely in my head. How on earth had I walked all the way to the riverbank?

Turn back! Quickly!

However, my body and my thoughts were moving in completely opposite directions, dragging me relentlessly toward the edge of the river despite my protests.

As I drew closer and closer to the red-walled, grey-tiled Dragon King Temple perched on the bank, a crisp sound of copper bells suddenly echoed from behind.

*Jingle, jingle, jingle...*

It was Granny's god-summoning bell!

With the ringing of those chimes, I felt a sudden, rebirth-like sensation as my soul rushed back into my body.

Realizing I had regained control of myself, I turned and bolted in the direction away from the riverbank, running and screaming at the top of my lungs, "Granny, I'm here!"

Granny was standing amid the withered reeds, her eyes tightly shut. Hearing my voice, she raised the god-summoning bell high and shook it violently to guide my way.

I scrambled back to her side, my hands and feet numb with cold, breathing in ragged, broken gasps.

Granny stripped off her thick, flower-patterned cotton-padded jacket and draped it over my shoulders, then grabbed my wrist and dragged me hurriedly toward home.

Once inside, I burrowed back onto the heated brick kang, wrapping myself in a thick quilt like a silkworm cocoon. Yet it did nothing to dispel the bone-deep chill inside me, and I shook with violent tremors.

Granny brewed a bowl of exceptionally strong, pungent ginger tea. I pinched my nose and forced it down, only then feeling slightly better, at least the shivering subsided.

"Granny, how did you know I was gone?" I asked tremblingly, huddled inside the duvet.

"The moment you pushed the door open and went out, I woke up," Granny said, her white, sightless eyes unblinking, her voice raspy. "I followed right behind you, shouting your name at the top of my lungs, but you didn't react at all. The whistling wind grew louder, and I realized you must be heading toward the riverbank.

In my desperation, I took out the soul-calling bell, trying to use it to snap you back to your senses.

Thank goodness, the gods saved you!"

I let out a slow, ragged breath. Thank goodness Granny had saved me.

"There is the fishy scent of a swamp on you... What on earth did you dream of?" Granny's tone turned grave.

I raised my arm and sniffed, but caught no unusual odor whatsoever.

Besides, there weren't even any swamps around our parts!

"Granny, I dreamed of the Dragon King. The Dragon King really did come for me!"

Too many things had happened over the past few days, and now I finally had the chance to recount the words from my dream to Granny.

Granny's expression grew increasingly ugly. Her sunken, sightless white eyes were hollow and lifeless, and her lips parted, muttering in a tongue of the Tungusic peoples that I couldn't comprehend.

I tentatively asked, "Granny, you say there's a Long Mingyuan and a Long Mingze; which of the two is the real Dragon King?"

Granny shook her head slightly, her low, raspy voice sounding profoundly bewildered. "I... cannot see. It is pitch black before my eyes. The gods are gradually withdrawing their divine power from me. All I can sense is that chilling, swampy aura about him, reeking of sin and danger..."

I felt a pang of worry regarding Granny's condition.

In the past, with deities lingering upon her, she merely needed to channel divine power to temporarily restore her sight.

She could even perceive many things invisible to ordinary mortals, such as... ghosts.

Yet now that her divine power had been stripped away, she had truly, completely become a blind old woman.

Worse still, she could no longer divine good and bad fortune, having lost her basic capacity for judgment.

Just as I was tearing my hair out over the riddle of the "true and false Dragon Kings," Granny suddenly reached out with her withered, eagle-claw-like hand and gripped my arm tightly.

"Jianlu, remember this: regardless of whether these two Dragon Kings are real or fake, both of them will drag you to your death..."

***

chapters.title: City Wall Earth
chapters.content:
"Last year, I cast a divination for you. The hexagram portended an extremely ominous doom. No matter which one of them has found you, be it true Dragon King or evil serpent, the outcome remains identical..." Granny closed her eyes, speaking with heavy dread.

"In the end, both of them will bring about your death!"

Granny's words left me utterly stunned, making me forget how to breathe.

Initially, I had been more inclined to trust Long Mingyuan. Especially after tonight, I increasingly felt that the one called Long Mingze possessed a crooked, sinister air that spelled deep trouble!

Yet Granny was telling me that both of them would kill me...

For a moment, I was completely at a loss. I couldn't hide, and I couldn't run!

Long Mingze had said that even if I fled to the ends of the earth, he would track me down.

I recalled the betrothal contract I had forged with the Dragon King even before I was born. Just as I was about to ask Granny what that was all about, I raised my gaze and saw that she had fallen asleep, leaning against the head of my bed.

Granny's physical condition was worsening by the day; her periods of deep sleep grew longer, while her waking moments grew ever shorter.

In our Northeast, there is a saying: the turn of the year is the gate of life and death.

Every winter is the hardest hurdle for the elderly to cross. If an old person can survive this long winter free from illness and disaster, it means they will live safely through the entire year.

Yet whenever the coldest days arrived, countless elderly folks failed to make it through, slipping away in haste.

Granny's current state terrified me. She had expended far too much divine power a few days ago delivering Liu Yazhi's baby, and moments earlier, she had stood out in the freezing wind for ages to save me. I couldn't help but worry whether she might fall ill.

I helped her onto the bed, curled up in her embrace just as I used to do when I was a child, and held her hand.

Silently, I prayed to the gods not to take away Granny's divine power, to grant me just a few more years so I could repay her kindness.

My mind raced with chaotic thoughts, yet my consciousness gradually drifted downward, and I fell asleep leaning against Granny.

When I opened my eyes, it was already ten in the morning. Glancing sideways, I saw that Granny was still fast asleep.

I got out of bed, fried two eggs for breakfast, left one for Granny, and then pulled on my coat to head over to Aunt Wang's place next door.

After a night had passed, I wondered if Wen Youcai and his wife had woken up yet.

Aunt Wang was sitting by the stove near her doorway, soling a shoe. Seeing me peer in from outside the gate, she waved and smiled. "Come on in, Jianlu. Are you here looking for your parents?"

Though my heart refused to acknowledge that title, I couldn't vent my anger on Aunt Wang, so I simply nodded.

Aunt Wang wore an expression of knowing understanding. "Last night's blizzard was far too fierce. Many livestock froze to death on the other side of the river. When those two heard about it, they worried about the dogs they kept in their courtyard and headed back at the crack of dawn."

Only then did I let out a sigh of relief.

It was good that they had gone back. Otherwise, I truly wouldn't have known how to face them.

In half a month, school would start. By then, I would take Granny back to school with me, and if those two wanted to find me again, it wouldn't be so easy.

"Thank you, Aunt Wang. I'll head back now," I said with genuine gratitude.

Instead, Aunt Wang called me back. "Wait a moment, Jianlu."

With that, she retreated into her house.

When she emerged again, she held a brown paper envelope in her hand. Judging by its thickness and shape, anyone could tell it was stuffed with a wad of cash.

"Your parents left this behind, telling me to hand it to you." Aunt Wang passed the envelope to me.

"No, I can absolutely not accept this!"

Since I had already refused to acknowledge them as parents, it meant making a clean break with those two from this day forward. How could I possibly take their money?

Aunt Wang sighed. "That's what I told them, too. I said you surely wouldn't want it. But that couple just dropped this package of money and bolted; I couldn't catch up to them even if I ran!

Keeping such a large sum of money doesn't feel right in my hands, so I can only pass it to you first. When you get a chance to see them in the future, just return it then."

With no other choice, I had to pocket the cash package.

Returning home, I opened the brown paper envelope. Inside, alongside a stack of crisp RMB banknotes, was a slip of paper bearing a string of addresses, precisely that of Dragon-Meeting Village across the river.

It seemed Wen Youcai and his wife still harbored the delusion that one day I would reconcile with them.

Without hesitation, I shoved the money into a drawer. When I passed by Dragon-Meeting Village before the start of the semester, I would drop it right back at Wen Youcai's doorstep; I didn't want to owe them even a shred of obligation.

Whether it was my imagination or not, the howling wind and blinding snow outside seemed to grow even more ferocious. The world outside was a sheet of stark white, with cotton-like snowflakes tumbling across the sky.

Suddenly, amidst this pale tempest, I caught sight of a solitary, trudging figure making their way toward our front gate.

Who could be so devoted?

To venture out in weather like this must take a bond thicker than blood!

As the figure drew closer, I recognized the marten-fur hat perched upon their head.

It was the village chief!

My heart skipped a beat, wondering if yet another crisis had broken out!

Before the chief could even knock, I opened the door to preempt him.

A flash of surprise crossed his face. Perhaps noting my unfriendly expression, he forced an ingratiating smile. "Jianlu, your grandmother..."

"She's not here," I coldly cut him off.

Over the years, the village chief had always treated Granny and me with utter neglect when times were good, only turning exceptionally obsequious whenever he needed a favor.

If Granny hadn't gone to deliver his grandson's baby and exhausted her vital energy, she wouldn't have been reduced to such a fragile state today.

The village chief was left speechless by my sharp rebuff. At that moment, however, Granny emerged from the room.

Seeing Granny sway slightly on her feet, I quickly stepped forward to support her, muttering under my breath, "Granny, the wind outside is so fierce, why did you come out!"

Granny squeezed my hand, then turned her attention to the chief. "Is something the matter?"

Looking somewhat sheepish, the village chief began, "Elder sister, you've seen it too, the weather anomalies this year. Ever since New Year's Eve, this heavy snow hasn't stopped for a single moment.

With the second day of the second lunar month fast approaching, if this keeps up, the crops and fruit trees will all be crushed by the snow. Living as we do tucked away in this mountain valley, if we lose our harvest next year, we'll all starve to death!

Added to that are the strange occurrences lately... The villagers are panic-stricken, convinced that some malevolent spirit is wreaking havoc!

A couple of days ago, someone tried to walk out of the village on foot, only to be blocked and turned back by the drifts.

He said something very peculiar: the further out toward the mountains he went, the heavier the snow became. Yet in the distance, far downstream where the riverwaters converged, the skies were clear and sunny, and the ice had already thawed!

Only our two villages are trapped beneath endless snowfall, as if... as if determined to keep someone here..."

The chief's words instantly made me think of Long Mingze.

Could it be... his doing?

Granny blinked her white, sightless eyes, asking with exhausted weariness, "What is it you want this old woman to do? Spit it out."

The village chief smiled awkwardly. "I'd like to ask elder sister to perform the god-dance once more."

"Not a chance in hell!" Before Granny could reply, I rejected him flatly, my face expressionless.

Granny's health had failed years ago. The last time she performed the dance was at the memorial rites for the village chief's mother, where she had fractured her ankle.

The doctor at the town hospital had said someone her age shouldn't go under the knife, so they had simply applied a plaster cast for basic treatment.

Ever since then, Granny walked with a limp and refused to perform the spirit dances for the villagers anymore.

Now that she was already this weak, how could she possibly have the stamina to dance the ritual sacrifice? Wasn't this just bullying an old widow and a defenseless girl?

chapters.title: White Wax Gold
chapters.content:
The village chief also knew he was being somewhat unreasonable, but he still smiled ingratiatingly and said, "I know Elder Sister is getting on in years, and logically speaking, I shouldn't come to bother you again, but I truly have no other choice!"

As he spoke, he let out a faint sigh. "First something happened to the youngest son of the Zhang family, and then there's that freak born to my Yazhi... The villagers are bound to think of evil spirits, feeling that the Dragon King has manifested his divine power!

Now everyone is trapped in the village, unable to go out or come in, letting their imaginations run wild all day and spreading groundless rumors. If this keeps up, something bad is going to happen!

Elder Sister, could I please ask you to perform the god-pleasing dance this time and ask for the will of the gods? As long as we can make this heavy snow stop, the whole village will slaughter pigs and sheep to make offerings for three days, right until the second day of the second lunar month!"

I bit my lower lip and said nothing more, feeling extremely anxious inside. What if... what if these bizarre phenomena were really aimed at me?

Granny pondered for a long time, then spoke indifferently, "I will dance."

"Granny!" I raised my eyes in surprise and looked at her.

Granny ignored me and said to the village chief, "Prepare yourselves. Gather at the village entrance stage at eight o'clock tonight."

"Thank you, Elder Sister! I was just waiting for these words from you!" The village chief left with profuse expressions of gratitude.

Filled with indignation, I urgently asked, "Granny, why did you agree to him? In your current state, you simply cannot perform the dance!"

Instead, Granny stroked the top of my head and let out a light sigh. "I am not doing this for the village chief; I am dancing for you. Right now, I can no longer receive the divine power of the gods and can do nothing. I must take advantage of the time before the gods go into hiding to invite a deity to possess my body so I can protect you.

Furthermore, I must ask the gods clearly about the candidate for the next shaman, to give them a head start in preparation so I can teach them everything I am able to.

I only hope that when I am no longer by your side, he will spare a thought for my sake as his master and do his utmost to protect you."

Hearing Granny say this, I couldn't help but throw myself into her arms and sob bitterly. "Granny, it's all my fault for being useless! If you hadn't picked me up, things wouldn't have come to this!"

Granny used her rough, wrinkled hands to wipe the tears from my face.

This sensation was far from pleasant, feeling like a washboard scraping across my tender skin, yet I still pressed my cheek into the palm of her hand and rubbed against it.

In a rare, gentle tone, Granny said, "Silly child, you were personally sent to me by the Deer God. Although I cannot see clearly what you went through in your past life, I know that our little Lu is definitely not an ordinary person, and that the blood of the deer spirit lineage flows through your body.

Your blessings lie ahead. When you achieve great wealth and high status in the future, you mustn't forget Granny!"

I laughed through my tears. "Don't worry, Granny! When I have money in the future, I will definitely show my filial piety to you!"

But I had to survive this year safely first.

The mere thought of Long Mingze gave me a headache. I went back inside the room to pack the ritual implements Granny would need for tonight's god-dancing ceremony.

Those items were locked by Granny inside the large, red-lacquered wooden chest at the bottom of the table.

During a special historical period, Granny was forced to bury sacred garments, ritual bells, and other implements deep within the Greater Khingan Mountains, thereby escaping disaster.

Yet no matter how many years had passed, the sacred garments remained incomparably brilliant, their dazzling and colorful flying-apsaras ribbons neither dull nor faded.

A shaman used many ritual implements, such as the copper bells at the waist, the hand drum, the sacred whip, and the haman knife, all of which were engraved with rich, colorful lines and symbols.

In particular, the shaman's mask depicted a mysterious and terrifying face with heavy, contrasting ink lines, featuring bold strokes and a ferocious expression.

The mask could be said to be everyone's first impression of shamanism, as well as an important element for experts studying Manchu-Mongolian culture.

Granny said these implements had the function of warding off evil spirits and expelling ghosts, while also serving as the shaman's patron deities.

As soon as she put on the sacred garment, the mask, and the sacred veil, she would be able to feel the guidance of the gods.

Naturally, she would dance along with the drumbeat in her hands, as if tireless, the more she danced, the more spirited she became.

After Granny finished washing up, I helped her put on the sacred garment.

This set of ritual implements was both heavy and cumbersome, weighing a total of over a hundred catties. The protective copper mirrors on the chest and the sacred skirt alone numbered over twenty.

When Granny's divine power was at its peak, she could wear this outfit and dance for five or six hours without feeling tired, but now, just as she finished dressing, I heard heavy, labored gasps coming from beneath the mask.

As I tied the buttons for her, I looked at her through the colorful-tasseled sacred veil and asked with concern, "Granny, do you really have to dance?"

She did not answer me, but instead put on her gloves, picked up the remaining ritual implements, and walked toward the village entrance stage.

With a quarter of an hour left until eight o'clock, the area beneath the stage was already bustling and crowded with people.

The heavy snow still showed no signs of stopping. Under the gloomy, dark sky, the wilderness was vast and silent.

The cold wind swept through the treetops, making a terrifying, sobbing sound, as if ghosts were weeping in some unseen place.

I supported Granny step by step up onto the stage, feeling her whole body trembling while she forced herself to put on a calm and composed appearance, her back and waist held straight.

Granny said her master had admonished her that from the very moment she put on the sacred garment, she was a deity and must stand loftily before the crowd in high spirits.

If she herself showed a weak and feeble appearance to others, who else would believe that she had invited the deities?

As soon as eight o'clock struck.

Granny raised her whip and struck the sacred drum in her hand, shaking her waist bells in time with the brisk drumbeat.

I matched her rhythm by beating the wooden clappers. Granny spun on her feet, her skirt billowing in the wind, her withered lips humming a melodious tune of the invitation to the gods.

Every shaman possessed a heaven-sent fine voice. In her youth, Granny's voice had been as melodious as an oriole's, but later, having sung the god-inviting chants too many times, her voice gradually grew hoarse.

Granny danced for half an hour until she was utterly exhausted, yet there was not the slightest sign of a deity possessing her. Seeing that her movements grew slower and slower with every dance, and that her lame foot constantly failed to exert force, I broke out in a cold sweat for her.

Beneath the stage, a little boy pointed at Granny and muttered, "Mom, when is this going to end? I want to go home and watch cartoons!"

Hearing this, I glanced over. The child's mother seemed to sense my displeased gaze, covered his mouth with her hand, and whispered, "Hush, don't talk nonsense!"

Yet, the expressions on the faces of the other villagers also grew impatient, and some even began to yawn.

Not only was the divine power in Granny's body gradually fading, but the gods in the people's hearts were also quietly disappearing.

Suddenly, Granny's footsteps paused, and her entire body froze in place.

Her pale pupils stared at me through the veiled mask, and from her eyes, I sensed intense panic and fear.

"Granny, what did you see?" For a moment, I even forgot to beat the clappers and asked in a daze.

Yet Granny continued to look at me with those pale, terrified eyes, her lips moving as she muttered in incomprehensible Tungus.

Then she closed her eyes, her body listed to one side, and she fell from the high stage like a stiff, dead butterfly...

"Granny!"

I cried out in alarm and hurriedly ran down the stage to Granny's side.

Removing the mask, I saw that Granny's face was pale and ashen, and two trails of blood and tears were flowing from the corners of her eyes. She had already lost consciousness.

***

chapters.title: Willow Wood
chapters.content:
I trembled as I tested her breathing with my hand. Fortunately, she was still breathing...

However, the stage was nearly two meters high, and Granny was already weak; falling from up there would likely result in at least a broken bone.

Not daring to move her casually, I cried out tearfully beside her ear, "Granny, Granny, wake up!"

The people around were whispering among themselves, having witnessed everything that just happened. With such an incident occurring during the god-worship ceremony, everyone felt deeply uneasy in their hearts.

The village chief squeezed through the crowd, shuddered when he saw the two trails of blood and tears on my grandmother's face, and then feigned composure as he said, "Human lives are at stake, save her first!"

Yet no one dared to approach my grandmother now; the village chief's words might as well have been blown into the wind.

In the end, it was Aunt Wang's husband who carried my grandmother back home on his back.

The clinic's doctor on duty was still in the town, unable to cross over due to the heavy snow blocking the roads.

The village chief had no choice but to invite a man who ran a medicine shop and had self-taught a little traditional Chinese medicine.

Whenever the villagers had minor ailments and were unwilling to go to the hospital, they would look to him for a few doses of herbal medicine to drink. People gave him the nickname "Wild Herbalist."

The Wild Herbalist came to the bedside to take my grandmother's pulse, squinted his eyes, shook his head, and pontificated, "Liver qi stagnation and heart-spleen disharmony; this is a sign of external evil invading the body!"

I stamped my feet in anxiety. "I don't understand the terms you're using. Just tell me straight, what on earth is wrong with my grandmother?"

The Wild Herbalist's expression changed, and he sheepishly said, "I can only make out that your grandmother's pulse is extremely weak, intermittent, and present one moment and gone the next, but this wasn't caused by physical trauma. As for why she remains unconscious...

Forgive my limited knowledge and superficial learning; you had better contact a doctor from the town hospital to come and take a look as soon as possible!"

The village chief was also provoked into a rage and cursed, "You've been talking for a long time and it's no different from saying nothing! With snow falling this heavily outside, cars simply can't drive through. If she could be sent to the town hospital, do you think I'd need to fetch a quack like you? Get the hell out of here!"

The Wild Herbalist snatched up his medicine box and fled as if escaping for his life.

Smoking a cigarette, the village chief looked at me with a helpless expression. "Xiaolu, don't be too upset yet. There's bound to be a way."

I wiped the tears from the corners of my eyes and said with firm resolve, "I'm going to the town to find a doctor!"

"It's nearly forty miles of mountain road from here to the town, and with the snow this deep, how is a girl like you going to make it?" the village chief asked in astonishment.

I glared at him fiercely. "If I don't go, am I just supposed to sit here and watch Granny lie here waiting to die?"

The village chief was left speechless by my retort.

My only family was Granny; it was she who had raised me through thrift and frugality, and even though she was blind, she still went up the mountains to dig for wild mountain goods to pay for my university tuition...

Everything she did was for my sake, and until her very last moment, she was still worrying about my destined trial. This deep kindness was something I could never repay.

With snow falling this heavily, no one wanted to step outside, and it was entirely possible I would freeze to death before even reaching the town.

But I really didn't want to lose Granny!

Seeing that he couldn't stop me, the village chief sighed and left.

I dug out my thickest down jacket and snow boots, wrapped myself tightly from head to toe with a hat and scarf, asked Aunt Wang next door to come over and help look after Granny, and stepped out the door without looking back.

As soon as I stepped out of the village, the wind and snow seemed to grow much heavier, and I made my way with difficulty toward the winding mountain road.

The biting cold wind felt like knives slicing across my cheeks, quickly numbing them with pain.

The accumulated snow on the ground was deeper than my knees, and every step felt as arduous as a pilgrimage. My feet had long since frozen to the point of unresponsiveness, leaving only a stubborn willpower to support my progress.

Yet the further I got from the village, the more violent the blizzard became.

The harsh, howling gale made it almost impossible for me to keep my eyes open. Snow blanketed the top of my head and my shoulders, and even my eyelashes were frosted with white, blurring my vision completely.

I panted heavily, sensing my body temperature slipping away bit by bit.

I cursed inwardly: If you have the ability, freeze me to death right here today!

Otherwise, even if I have to crawl, I will crawl all the way to the town and bring back a doctor to save my grandmother!

Suddenly, I heard Aunt Wang shouting from behind.

"Xiaolu, Xiaolu..."

I turned my head and saw Aunt Wang stumbling toward me, waving her hand and calling out, "Xiaolu, you don't need to go to the hospital! The moment you left, your grandmother woke up!"

"Really?" I was overjoyed.

"Your grandmother was speaking Manchu; I couldn't understand it and didn't know what she was saying. Hurry back with me and take a look." Aunt Wang's expression was extremely solemn, making it clear that Granny's condition was still far from optimistic.

Granny had suddenly fallen from the stage, and before losing consciousness, she had looked at me with that kind of gaze; something must have happened.

After thinking it over, I decided to return with Aunt Wang first.

Aunt Wang had run after me all the way just now and must have been quite exhausted. I felt that her footsteps were a bit weak, and she remained silent on the return journey.

Fortunately, the closer we got to Longshou Village, the lighter the blizzard became. The goose-feather snowflakes on the winding mountain road had turned into a gentle, swirling snow, and I finally caught my breath.

"Aunt Wang, thank you for braving such heavy snow to come find me. Later on, I'll help tutor your youngest son with his schoolwork," I said with deep gratitude.

Aunt Wang remained silent, lowering her head and continuing to walk forward. "Hmm..."

I suddenly realized that Aunt Wang was acting a bit strange today!

Normally, Aunt Wang talked a lot. As long as you were with her, her mouth never stayed idle.

Even if you showed a lack of interest, she would still pull you along and chatter endlessly.

Yet walking the entire way just now, Aunt Wang hadn't said a single word, and even when I took the initiative to speak to her, she couldn't be bothered to respond.

How truly bizarre!

Filled with doubt, I followed behind her for nearly another mile.

Raising my head abruptly, a patch of reeds as tall as a person appeared before my eyes. The withered yellow stalks had been bent considerably by the fierce wind, revealing the wide, calm surface of the river not far away.

And on the opposite bank of the river stood that dilapidated Dragon King Temple with its grey walls and red tiles!

I immediately stopped in my tracks, my head buzzing as I felt the chill seep into my marrow.

Aunt Wang turned around and said breathlessly, "Xiaolu, why are you standing still? Hurry up, we're almost home!"

I still didn't budge, but Aunt Wang continued walking toward the riverside, not forgetting to wave at me.

"Xiaolu, hurry over here!"

There was something wrong with this Aunt Wang!

Everyone in the village avoided that Dragon King Temple like the plague, so how could Aunt Wang bring me to the Dragon King Temple in the middle of the night?

Unless she wasn't "Aunt Wang" at all!

Without time to think too much, I turned around and ran back along the mountain road I had just come from.

Noticing I hadn't followed, "Aunt Wang" called out from behind, "Xiaolu, where are you going? Hurry back!"

I'm not going back to the Dragon King Temple with you!

Running continuously for two miles until I could no longer see "Aunt Wang's" figure, I finally stopped.

My whole body felt limp, and I collapsed into the snow to rest for a moment.

Yet when I opened my eyes again, a familiar face appeared in my field of vision, smiling genially down at me.

"Xiaolu, I've finally found you!"

This sight made me draw in a sharp breath of cold air...

How could there be another Wang...

chapters.title: Water in the Spring
chapters.content:
"Xiaolu, hurry back with Auntie, something happened at your house!" Aunt Wang called out in her shrill voice.

I, however, stood frozen in the snowbank, unable to move.

Where on earth did this Aunt Wang pop up from?

"Xiaolu, didn't you hear me? Why are you still sitting here, frozen stupid?"

I don't know if my ears had gone bad from the cold, but Aunt Wang's voice blended into the wind and snow, sounding somewhat ethereal.

My heartstrings were taut as I asked, "Aunt Wang, did my grandmother wake up?"

"Your grandmother hasn't woken up. Who told you she woke up?" Aunt Wang's expression turned surprised. "A rather young man came to your yard, shouting that he wants to see you!"

Hearing this, I frowned.

Over the years, Granny had kept strict watch over me, and the men in the village avoided me like the plague. Who would run over to look for me in the middle of the night?

"Auntie, did you see that man's appearance clearly? What does he look like?"

"Oh, my, that look is so handsome! And that figure, *tsk tsk*! He looks like he walked right out of a painting...

He even claimed to be your fiancé. Well done, Xiaolu, you found such a good-looking partner and didn't even tell Auntie!" Aunt Wang's mouth curved into a teasing smile.

Fiancé?

It was already midnight. Could it be that Long Mingze had come to my house to find me?

Could he have done something to my grandmother?

Thinking of this, I didn't dare to delay any longer. I nimbly crawled up from the snow and patted my backside. "Then Aunt Wang, let's hurry back!"

Aunt Wang gave a sound of assent and walked ahead to lead the way.

Along the way, my head was filled with images of Long Mingze.

Didn't he say he was still in a dormant state and could only visit me in dreams, unable to manifest his true form?

Yet, I wasn't dreaming right now!

Suddenly, my foot stepped on a piece of ice, and I nearly tumbled off the cliff. Fortunately, Aunt Wang had quick eyes and fast hands, and she caught me.

"Xiaolu, why aren't you watching where you walk? If you fell down there, you'd lose your life!" she casually admonished.

I was about to thank her when I felt that her hand felt somewhat strange to the touch. "Thank you, Wan... Auntie?"

It didn't have the tactile sensation that human skin should have. The pads of her fingers felt loose and flaccid when pressed, lacking both warmth and the elasticity of muscle tissue.

It was as if it were a piece of... straw paper?

What shocked me even more was that just now, Aunt Wang had been walking ahead of me, a distance of nearly two or three meters away. How had she instantly transferred to my side?

Could her true identity not be a rural middle-aged woman, but a successor of the Wudang Sect?

Aunt Wang seemed to sense my distraction as well. She quickly pulled back her hand, cast a somewhat stiff smile at me, and continued walking forward.

I felt that I was mostly likely frozen stupid, and my train of thought was starting to malfunction.

I raised a hand and patted my face, trying to clear my head a little bit.

Yet the scene before my eyes almost scared my soul right out of my body...

Aunt Wang was still moving forward slowly. With such heavy snow falling, her figure didn't show the slightest bit of stumbling or struggle; instead, it looked more like she was floating.
