What was most spine-chilling was that when I looked back at the mountain path the two of us had walked along, there were only my own set of footprints, deeply branded into the snow...

Abruptly, the wind at my ears grew fiercer, and I felt waves of chilly air drilling into the back of my collar.

I slowly turned my head, only to come face-to-face with a paper doll whose facial features were drawn with heavy, thick ink!

The paper doll was even wearing Aunt Wang's military cotton-padded overcoat. The eyebrows and eyes outlined in black ink were smiling broadly, and its paper mouth opened and closed, emitting a shrill pitch, "Xiaolu, why aren't you walking anymore?"

Oh mother, whose paper doll floated out on its own?

Which ghost brotherly brother, please do me a favor and hurry up and lead your wife back home!

I mustered all the strength I had sucked from my mother to run backward. The paper doll's bright red lips emitted a "he-he-he" eerie laugh as it floated toward me again.

"Xiaolu, stop running, come with me! He-he-he..."

My feet had long since gone numb from the cold, and being startled by this paper doll made them even more disobedient, causing me to tumble down into the snow once more.

The paper doll reached out her ghostly claws, pale and withered like dead branches, and grabbed at me. I couldn't dodge in time, and she scratched five large rips into my down jacket.

Pure white duck down fluttered out from inside, dancing in front of my eyes along with the snowflakes.

The paper doll still refused to let up, reaching her claws toward me again...

At the same time my sweater was torn open, a dazzling beam of golden light shot straight out from my chest, dispelling the darkness for a radius of several miles.

"Ah-ah-ah..."

A miserable shriek came from the paper doll's mouth. The hand that had just touched me unexpectedly burst into tiny flames.

Since it was made of paper to begin with, those flames instantly spread upward along its arm, turning into a towering blaze.

That bizarre face was scorched and gradually distorted before my eyes. In just a few seconds, it had burned into a pile of ash.

I snapped out of my terror, reached out, and felt my chest. My fingertips brushed against a rhombus-shaped object.

It was the black piece of jade Long Mingyuan had given me!

After waking up from that dream that day, I had drilled a hole in this thing and wore it around my neck on a red string.

I originally wanted to use it as a protective amulet for good luck, but I didn't expect this thing to actually work!

Long Mingyuan hadn't lied to me...

I tremblingly climbed up from the snow, looking with lingering fear at the pitch-black mountain road ahead.

In that patch of darkness, it was as if something wanted to stop me and keep me from leaving Dragon Guardian Village!

Meanwhile, there was a large hole torn in my chest, letting the chilling wind whistle in, and my body temperature was continuing to drop.

I had to get home as quickly as possible, or I would freeze to death in this deep mountain!

A person's will to survive in a time of crisis is terrifyingly strong. I made two steps out of three and returned to the village in less than half an hour.

As a result, at the village entrance, I saw 'Aunt Wang' again...

"Xiaolu, what's wrong with you? Seeing that we were about to reach the village entrance, why did you turn around and run away? And you ran so fast I couldn't even catch up; it worked me to death!" Aunt Wang leaned against the large willow tree at the village entrance and complained, looking like she truly was exhausted.

How could this still be endless!

If the 'Aunt Wang' from just a moment ago was fake, then this one right before my eyes should be real?

Crouching slightly, I approached her by two steps and asked vigilantly, "Auntie, you... are you human?"

Aunt Wang glared fiercely at me, exasperated. "How does a child like you talk? If I'm not human, what else could I be?"

Taking advantage of the fact that she wasn't prepared, I reached out my hand and quickly patted her face.

Warm...

She was the real Aunt Wang!

Yet Aunt Wang was left utterly bewildered by my action, staring at me in a daze.

Just as she wanted to open her mouth to scold me, she caught sight of the large hole torn in the front of my chest and said in astonishment, "How did this happen? Hurry home, I'll get some needle and thread to patch it for you."

Supported by her as we walked toward my courtyard, my heartbeat, which had been panicked the entire night, finally calmed down. I asked, "Auntie, why did you lead me toward the direction of the Dragon King Temple just now?"

"Oh my, wasn't I worried that something might happen to your grandmother, and thinking we should get back sooner!" Aunt Wang said indifferently.

"Going across the river surface takes a shortcut. Following that abandoned path by the entrance of the Dragon King Temple to return to the village is at least twenty minutes faster. Otherwise, you think I'd want to poke around that unlucky place in the middle of the night?"

chapters.title: Earth on the Roof
chapters.content:
"Then why didn't you speak at all along the way, Auntie?" I asked cautiously again.

"Didn't your grandmother tell you that you can't open your mouth when walking in the winter?" Aunt Wang rolled her eyes with a helpless expression. "The snow in the mountains is so big, if you open your mouth you'll swallow a belly full of wind. I don't want to get the runs!"

I was completely speechless. This false alarm had almost cost me my life at the hands of a paper doll. Fortunately, Long Mingyuan's protective talisman had saved me!

Mentioning Long Mingyuan, I always felt that he truly wanted to save me.

Yet Granny said that he would kill me...

Arriving back home, I took off my tattered down jacket and ran straight to Granny's bed.

Granny still kept her eyes tightly shut, lying flat on the bed, but her lips were constantly moving.

Leaning my ear close to listen, I found that the word she kept murmuring over and over was the exact same.

The Tungus vocabulary I had learned wasn't much, but Granny had just happened to teach me that word.

She was saying, Lu (Deer).

I thought Granny was calling me, so I grasped her hand and called out in a low voice, "Granny, I'm here. What do you want?"

However, Granny had no other consciousness beyond this; her mouth was still continuously murmuring, "Lu, Lu..."

My mood plummeted once more, and I leaned against the head of the bed, not knowing what to do.

Aunt Wang, however, frowned and said, "Xiaolu, why do I feel like your grandmother's condition doesn't seem quite right?"

I looked at her blankly. "What's not right about it?"

"She doesn't look like she suddenly fell into a coma due to some major illness; rather, it looks... like she's lost her soul!"

Aunt Wang carefully scrutinized my grandmother's complexion. "My son had a similar situation before. He went to play in the back mountains with a group of kids, and when he came back he started falling into a coma, talking in his sleep, and babbling nonsense!"

In the back mountains, there was a potter's field (graveyard for paupers/unclaimed bodies) with a history even older than our village. Some people said they had seen tombs from the Xianbei period inside.

Some of the lonely elderly people in the village, when they died without anyone to manage their funerals, were also uniformly buried in the potter's field.

Since childhood, I had heard many ghost legends about the potter's field, and there were also male classmates in my class who didn't know any better and proposed going there to test their courage.

Granny, however, had said that the place had very heavy *yin* energy and not to approach it casually.

Aunt Wang continued, "At that time, I took him to the clinic, but the doctor couldn't make out anything proper. He gave him an antipyretic injection, but the boy still didn't wake up.

I could only ask your grandmother to come take a look. She said my son had lost his soul, led him to that graveyard in the back mountains, and shook a divine bell for half the night before finally summoning his soul back!"

If it was truly as Aunt Wang said, that my grandmother had lost her soul, but I hadn't inherited Granny's witchcraft and didn't know how to call back a soul!

Aunt Wang pondered for a moment, then suddenly thought of something. "Hey, doesn't a person surnamed Ma live at the end of our village? Why not let him come take a look at your grandmother?"

The person Aunt Wang mentioned was named Ma Zhengliang. He was in his forties and still a bachelor, a *dima* (shamanic spirit medium), whom we all called Uncle Ma.

He enshrined a complete pantheon at his home, the Hu, Huang, Chang, and Mang (Fox, Weasel, Yellow-crested Snake, and Python), along with the Qingfeng and Beiwang (ghosts/spirits).

That Uncle Ma knew how to conduct himself well. Believing that my village already had my grandmother holding down the fort for divinations and readings, he had proactively moved his spirit hall to the end of the village.

*Chuma* (horse-riding/spirit mediumship) has similarities with Shamanism, but they are not the same lineage.

Shamanism is a type of witchcraft, worshipping all natural things and totems.

While *chuma* is more like borrowing elements from Shamanism, Taoism, and Buddhism to independently establish a system, belonging to a form of folk culture.

Shamanism has been passed down since the ancient fishing and hunting period, whereas *chuma* only has a history of a little over 300 years.

Yet it has to be said that in recent years, the reputation of *chuma* has become much louder than that of Shamanism, simply because the conditions for inheriting Shamanism are too harsh, emphasizing bloodline inheritance. Without this bloodline, one cannot learn it, and it cannot be changed.

I pondered for a while, but still decided to go find that Uncle Ma to ask. If that didn't work, I'd go to the township hospital.

Uncle Ma's hall was very remote, located at the end of the village near the foot of the mountain, far away from the center of the village, and he never proactively interacted with people.

I stepped forward and knocked on the door. Uncle Ma seemed to have guessed that I would come over, and welcomed me inside with a smile.

The hall was decorated very prettily. Desks and tables were lined with statues of deities from left to right, and an extremely alluring painting of the Nine-Tailed Fox Immortal hung on the wall.

Fresh fruit platters and flowers were placed at the front.

"I have another guest here right now. Could you please wait a moment?" Uncle Ma negotiated with me in a good-tempered manner.

I signaled for him to go ahead with his business first, as I also wanted to see what abilities this Uncle Ma actually possessed.

Uncle Ma comforted me to sit down on the sofa, then turned around and walked back into the inner room.

Through the old-fashioned glass paper window, I could see that a middle-aged woman was also lying on the bed in the inner room, her hand pressed against her temples, her brow deeply furrowed.

She had probably suffered a headache, and since the clinic wasn't open, she could only come to Uncle Ma for emergency relief.

Through that crack, I saw Uncle Ma tilt his head, whisper something to the empty air beside him, and spread open his palm.

After a few seconds, a pack of traditional Chinese medicine materialized out of thin air in his palm!

Was this the ability of *chuma*, fetching medicine from thin air?

While I was astonished, I also felt somewhat joyous; Granny should be saved!

The woman left in a hurry after getting her medicine, and Uncle Ma walked out as well.

The air in the room didn't circulate well, permeated by the scent of incense burning year-round that refused to dissipate. Fortunately, Granny also frequently lit incense at home, so I was long used to this smell.

"You came to ask about your grandmother, right?" Uncle Ma's teeth were slightly yellowish as he grinned and said.

I nodded. "Uncle Ma, can you take a look and see what on earth is wrong with my grandmother?"

"I heard about what happened tonight. Logically speaking, your grandmother has deities protecting her, so how could this happen?" Uncle Ma poured a cup of chrysanthemum tea and handed it to me.

I didn't drink it, instead holding it in the palm of my hand to warm myself, and choked out, "My grandmother... is going to undergo divine concealment (passing away/abandoning her mortal shell)."

Uncle Ma let out an understanding sigh. "No wonder... Then let me ask the immortals and see if they have a way."

A short while later, Uncle Ma lit twelve full-hall incense sticks for those deity statues, then closed his eyes and sat cross-legged on a nearby reed mat.

The room fell silent, with only those twelve incense sticks burning silently.

I had never witnessed the scene of *chuma* immortals possessing a medium's orifices, and just as I wanted to step forward to observe closely, Uncle Ma suddenly shivered all over, twitching on the reed mat like an epileptic.

When he opened his eyes again, his gaze had become a bit dazed and bewitching, sweeping toward me languidly, "Oh, this little sister's background is no small matter!"

Startled, I didn't dare to make a sound, leaning my body back against the sofa.

Uncle Ma's voice had grown shrill, and he hooked his orchid-shaped fingers to cover his mouth as he chuckled, "Hehe, don't be afraid! Granny Hu here never harms people!"

Only then did I understand that Uncle Ma had been possessed by the fox immortal enshrined in his hall, and the one speaking right now should be that Nine-Tailed Fox hanging on the wall.

"Little sister, your birth characters (bazi) bear a bone weight of four taels and eight qian, which should make you a person of great wealth and nobility. Unfortunately, your life has tribulations, and these tribulations have accompanied you from the very moment you were born.

In order to help you avoid disaster, your grandmother reversed the year pillar of your bazi, which caused bad luck to entangle you and all your affairs to go against you!

Only by peacefully surviving this tribulation can you restore your original fate destiny."

chapters.title: Thunderbolt
chapters.content:
Uncle Ma looked big and rough on the outside, bearing the distinct physical traits of a Manchu man, yet he was currently speaking in the voice of an Eastern Depot eunuch. It made me feel extremely uncomfortable.

"This tribulation of yours, I cannot help you with. I'm afraid no one can help you; you can only cross it by yourself!"

"Hu, Granny Hu, I'm not here to ask about myself, I'm here to ask about my grandmother! She..." Before I could finish, Uncle Ma interrupted me.

"No need to say more!" Uncle Ma made a stopping gesture at me. "I know what you want to ask, little sister. Your grandmother's soul has been extracted by a very powerful entity, and I cannot afford to offend him!"

Disregarding my nervousness, I hurriedly pressed on, "Who is the entity that extracted my grandmother's soul?"

Uncle Ma gave a seductive glance, dragging out his tone, "That I cannot tell you. Otherwise, if he comes looking for me, I won't be able to handle it either."

I was so anxious tears were about to fall. He twisted his waist and lightly hummed, "Alright, alright, I know your Granny Hu can't bear to watch a beauty cry. Trying this routine on me, are you?

I can only tell you this: that entity is related to you by blood, flowing with the exact same blood as you!"

Related by blood?

Aside from Granny, I had no other family!

Suddenly, I recalled the couple who had come looking for me a couple of days ago, claiming to be my biological parents, Wen Youcai and his wife...

Could it be them?

'Uncle Ma' raised his hand, as if wanting to touch his own flawless face, but ended up feeling a handful of stubble, a look of disgust crossing his features.

"Go quickly, little sister. You must find your grandmother's soul within a month. Otherwise, your grandmother's physical body will die, rot, and smell... By then, no matter what you do, it will be too late!"

Just as I was about to open my mouth to ask for more clues, Uncle Ma had already returned to normal.

He shook his head, his gaze becoming clear again, and said earnestly, "Immortal immortals also value affinity when handling matters. Since they say they can't help, we shouldn't force it.

However, the immortal has at least pointed a path for you. You might as well go back first and think about it: among those blood-related relatives of yours, who would harm your grandmother?"

Aside from Wen Youcai and his wife, I couldn't think of anyone else for the time being.

That day, when Granny refused to accept the money Wen Youcai handed over, I had caught a trace of ruthlessness on his face.

Perhaps out of fear that Granny was a Shaman, or perhaps not wanting to leave a bad impression on me, he hadn't erupted on the spot.

But I could sense that this couple, Wen Youcai and his wife, were no good.

It was entirely possible that in order to make me acknowledge them, they had hired some other evil entity to extract Granny's soul!

I thanked Uncle Ma, left him some incense money, and got up to leave the spirit hall.

Whether from being smoked by the incense for too long or from not sleeping all night, my head felt dizzy and heavy, and I even forgot how I walked home.

Seeing me in such a soul-deprived state, Aunt Wang asked in a low voice, "Xiaolu, what did that man named Ma say?"

My expression was exceptionally heavy. "Granny's soul wasn't lost; it was extracted by something else!"

Fear surfaced in the depths of Aunt Wang's eyes. "Then what do we do?"

Having taken in the cold wind all the way back, my head finally cleared up a bit. Ignoring Aunt Wang's question, I turned aside and ran into the bedroom.

I opened the drawer of the bedside table and took out the kraft paper envelope.

A thick stack of red banknotes tumbled to the ground, mixed with a slip of paper bearing the Wen family's address.

I bent down to pick up the slip of paper, a cold sneer seeping from the corner of my mouth.

That morning, they had left so decisively that I thought they had given up.

It turned out they had already left a backup plan, forcing me to take the initiative and come to them!

I tucked the pack of money into my bosom, went out, and said to Aunt Wang, "Auntie, I need to make a trip to Dragon-Meeting Village across the river. As for Granny, I'm afraid I'll have to trouble you to keep an eye on her."

Aunt Wang was sitting in front of our brick-bed, soleing a pair of shoes for her son. Hearing this, she readily agreed, "Go ahead with peace of mind, I'm here."

Pushing open the courtyard gate, a corner of my down jacket was whipped up by the cold wind, the chill piercing.

Yet compared to the previous night, the daytime wind and snow had lessened considerably.

The sky hung low and overcast, shrouding the silver-frosted river surface.

Unable to approach the Dragon King Temple, I simply detracted through the mountain woods, walking for a full hour before finally reaching Dragon-Meeting Village on the opposite bank.

Following the address on the slip of paper Wen Youcai gave me, I discovered that the most imposing small foreign-style building in the entire village was their home.

While everyone else lived in low, single-story flat houses, theirs was a three-story European-style villa, with a courtyard even larger than the village chief's.

As I approached the gate, a Rottweiler barked frantically at me through the iron fence.

"Woof woof..."

This breed of dog was extremely ferocious, capable of fighting wolves and guarding cattle.

Wild beasts often roamed our mountainous area, and wealthy families would raise one or two fierce dogs to prevent black bears from visiting.

However, if such dogs were not properly trained, they would never let go once they bit someone.

Staring at the Rottweiler, I nervously stepped back two paces.

At that moment, a crisp, coquettish female voice came from inside the gate, "Benben, stop barking, or I'll stew you into dog meat soup!"

The vicious dog actually stopped barking, tucked its tail, and scurried back to its kennel.

A moment later, a girl around my age walked out of the villa.

She was dressed very fashionably, wearing a burgundy knee-length dress that exposed her slender, straight calves encased in a layer of skin-toned fake-translucent tights. Her Chanel-style double-faced woolen overcoat was even adorned with a few pearls.

Her appearance could be described as pretty: willow-leaf eyebrows, phoenix eyes, and exquisite makeup.

Her eyelids were brushed with a layer of glittering eyeshadow, and her lipstick was a bewitching, vibrant shade of red.

Every gesture of hers reeked of spoiled haughtiness, like a pampered little princess.

"Who are you looking for?" The girl seemed to be complaining about me summoning her out in this freezing weather, her tone somewhat displeased.

I withdrew my gaze, stepped forward, and asked, "Do Wen Youcai and Fu Hongmei live here?"

The girl arched her eyebrows, her posture arrogant. "Are you looking for my parents for something?"

I was stunned, my voice dropping hoarsely, "They are your... parents?"

Wouldn't that make the person in front of me my...

The girl seemed to realize something as well, looking me up and down with astonishment. "You're Lin Jianlu? My, older sister, whom I've never met!"

The word "sister" rolled off her tongue, but the meaning had changed, carrying a heavy dose of disgust and, even more so, mockery.

"Mom said a girl would come looking for us these past few days. So it's you!" A look of disdain surfaced in the depths of her eyes, and she sneered.

"You know about me?" I felt as though I had been cast into a boundless, deep sea, my blood freezing into ice all over.

Crossing her arms, she looked supremely arrogant. "Of course I know you, Lin Jianlu!

Look at that poverty-stricken appearance of yours, wearing nothing but rags, not a single designer brand on your whole body. Including your underwear, it probably doesn't even add up to two hundred yuan, right?

To have an identical twin sister like you is just mortifying!"

The shrill, haughty voice entered my ears like a sudden clap of thunder bursting forth.

I had thought this girl was a second child born after Wen Youcai and the others abandoned me; I never expected us to be identical twins...

Logically speaking, identical twins were cut from the same mold, with a very high degree of similarity, sometimes even biological parents couldn't tell them apart.

Yet, to say this girl and I looked identical would be a stretch; it was more like we had no resemblance at...

chapters.title: Pine and Cypress Wood
chapters.content:
She had a pair of slender, alluring phoenix eyes, while I had large apricot-shaped eyes.

Our temperaments and dispositions could likewise be said to be complete opposites.

That bright and striking face was full of meanness and arrogance, while I felt that such an attitude lacked all upbringing.

If the two of us were to walk down the street side-by-side, we certainly wouldn't be recognized as biological sisters.

Now I began to wonder: was that birth certificate fake?

Or perhaps the Wen family had taken the wrong baby, which was why they threw me into the woods...

The girl who claimed to be my younger sister spoke again, her tone still contemptuous, "Why aren't you talking? Are you mute? Didn't you refuse quite readily before?

Saying things like 'I want to stay with Granny and completely cut ties with the Wen family'; I actually thought a little better of you back then!

Now that you know how good having money feels, you've decided to abandon your poor grandmother and come over here for a free meal?"

My gaze darkened. Just as I was about to retort a couple of times, Fu Hongmei walked out the door.

"Baby, who are you talking to in this freezing weather?"

When she saw me standing behind the gate, her expression froze slightly, followed by a blossom of joy on her face.

"Xi... Xiaolu, it really is you!" She opened the gate, reached out, and pulled me in. "What are you doing standing outside? Come inside quickly!"

I thought to myself: I'd love to go inside, but your precious daughter has to let me!

Sure enough, seeing Fu Hongmei hugging me and walking toward the house, Younger Sister's face turned as ugly as the heavy clouds blanketing the sky.

The interior decoration of the foreign-style building was extremely luxurious, with dark gold as the main color scheme, flashy yet somewhat tacky.

The furniture, such as the tables and sofas, was also a dirt-yellow color. The Wen family seemed eager to replace even their tableware with pure gold, fully displaying the style of upstarts.

I coldly swept my gaze around the surroundings, and amidst the astonishment, I also felt a bit puzzled.

Since the Wen family was so wealthy, why didn't they move away from the mountainous area and buy a sea-view villa in Hainan? Why insist on enduring hardship in these deep, isolated mountains?

Fu Hongmei handed me a fruit plate. "Xiaolu, you must be hungry, right? Have some fruit to pad your stomach first, and tonight I'll make a few more of my signature dishes for you to try."

The plate was filled with fruits I had never eaten before: cherries, Shine Muscat grapes, wax apples.

There was even a fruit that looked like a green toad and didn't look appetizing at all... Later I learned that kind of fruit was called a sugar-apple.

These fruits weren't cheap in the Northeast. When I was in school, I had seen them at Yuanda Supermarket; the price of a single catjin (half a kilo) was enough for me to eat at the cafeteria for several days.

Seeing this, Younger Sister scoffed, "I just love seeing this country-bumpkin look of yours!"

"Wen Ting, say a little less!" Fu Hongmei scolded her in a low voice.

The girl named Wen Ting curled her lips in utter indifference.

Ignoring the fruit plate, I asked indifferently, "Can I see that birth certificate again?"

Fu Hongmei's expression stalled, but she quickly adjusted. "Okay, wait a moment, I'll go get it for you."

After she left, only Wen Ting and I were left in the living room.

Sitting on the other side of the sofa and fiddling with her fingernails, Wen Ting said offhandedly, "You suspect you're not Mom's biological daughter, don't you?"

I didn't answer her.

"No need to doubt it!" Wen Ting looked at me with a provocative gaze. "All these years, our whole family has always known of your existence. When you were in middle school, I even went to your school to look for you!"

I raised my head in shock, "You went to look for me? Why don't I remember..."

"I didn't appear in front of you; I just secretly observed you through the iron railing. You were just as poor and shabby as I imagined!" She lowered her voice considerably, as if afraid of being overheard by Fu Hongmei.

"Eating five-cent popsicles without cream, wearing a faded school uniform, and not even wanting to replace your school bag when it got a hole!"

I coldly watched this "younger sister" who had suddenly appeared. No matter how composed I tried to appear on the outside, inside I was shaken to the core.

So I had always lived under the surveillance of the Wen family!

For these past twenty years, none of them wanted to acknowledge me, so why had their attitude suddenly changed now?

At that moment, Fu Hongmei and Wen Youcai walked out of the room together, bringing not only my birth certificate but Wen Ting's as well.

I discovered that the time of birth between Wen Ting and me was less than ten minutes apart.

"When I gave birth to you two back then, the fetal position was abnormal, so I opted for a C-section. You were the first one pulled out, and the nurse said you cried louder than any other baby, so you'd definitely have a strong mind!" Fu Hongmei smiled.

"That's why I named you Wen Wan, hoping you'd be gentle and compliant... Sigh, that nurse really didn't miss the mark; you really do have a strong mind!" Wen Youcai sighed.

I returned the birth certificate to them. With ironclad facts before my eyes, I had nothing left to doubt.

Precisely because Fu Hongmei had been carrying identical twins and birthed two at once, household expenses had surged sharply, and there wasn't even enough breast milk to go around.

Both husband and wife had been laid off at the same time, leaving them without a source of income, adding frost to the snow for an already non-affluent family.

And since I had been diagnosed with congenital asthma, they chose to abandon me.

Anyway, without me, they still had a physically sound daughter, Wen Ting.

By sacrificing me alone, the family of three could survive!

At this thought, the tears I had been holding back finally broke free. Gritting my teeth, I asked, "Since you already had one precious daughter, why come looking for me!"

Seeing that I had guessed the reason, Wen Youcai simply abandoned all pretense. "Xiaotong is going abroad for her studies next semester, a combined bachelor's and master's program, and she doesn't plan to come back after graduation, striving to get a green card and stay abroad to develop.

Your mother's and my businesses are both domestic, so we can't go abroad to accompany her.

That's why we thought about bringing you back, first, to have a daughter by our side to keep us company, and second, to hand over our family company for you to manage, which can be considered making up for the debt we owe you all these years."

This speech sounded quite sincere, far more moving than the forced affection at Granny's house that day.

Yet they had abandoned me for money back then, and now they wanted to trick me back with money; how could it be that easy!

"Don't make it sound so nice, handing the company over to me, making up for debts... Isn't it just finding someone to take care of you in your old age, and the kind of person who works without complaint and comes at the snap of a finger!"

I pulled the kraft paper envelope from my bosom, slammed it heavily onto the table, and said with an indifferent tone, "This is the money you left behind. Count it; not a single bill should be missing!

Take your stinking money back. I don't want this cheap family affection, and don't even think about using moral concepts to kidnap me!

I'll say it again: the relationship between you and me ended the moment you decided to abandon me!"

Neither Wen Youcai nor his wife expected me to come here just to return the money. Even Wen Ting looked at me with an expression of astonishment.

"Xiaolu, this money was meant to be living expenses we left for you, considered a bit of compensation from your mother and me. Lin Granny has run into trouble now, and this is precisely when you'll need money. You should still take it!" Wen Youcai coaxed with a good temper.

I abruptly raised my eyes, sweeping a cold gaze over them. "How do you know my grandmother ran into trouble?"

chapters.title: Long-Flowing Water
chapters.content:
Wen Youcai and his wife were startled, saying in bewilderment, "Granny Lin fell off the stage while performing the sacrificial god dance and is now unconscious. Such a huge deal, the whole village was buzzing about it since last night!"

I asked sternly, "Did you two do something to my grandmother?"

Wen Youcai looked innocent. "We didn't do anything!"

"Wasn't it you who pulled some tricks and hooked my grandmother's soul away during the sacrifice?" I looked at their expressions and continued to probe.

"How would ordinary folks like us know any soul-snatching black magic? You think everyone is as much of a charlatan as that grandmother of yours!" Wen Ting rolled her eyes at me, and was pinched by Fu Hongmei.

I saw that their expressions didn't seem fake.

If Granny's matter really had anything to do with them, they wouldn't have this attitude right now; instead, they would be starting to negotiate terms with me.

Yet the fox immortal said that the creature who snatched my grandmother's soul had the same blood flowing in its veins as me.

Could it be that I have other relatives in this world?

I threw out this doubt, but Wen Youcai shook his head. "No more. The elders in the family passed away one after another the year you were born..."

From Wen Youcai's words, I learned that this branch of the Wen family ultimately left only Wen Ting and me.

I fell into confusion once again, the clue given by the fox immortal ending right here.

"Xiaolu, we know you're worried about Granny Lin, but don't let your imagination run wild!

We have a private doctor in our family; he lives in the village downstream. Let him go examine Granny Lin first tomorrow, figure out what illness she actually has, and then you'll have a bottom line in your mind."

Fu Hongmei spoke words of comfort and gave Wen Youcai a look.

"Yes, yes, that doctor is very capable! Previously, Xiaotang had a persistent high fever, and he cured it as soon as he arrived!" Wen Youcai quickly echoed.

I completely lost my bearings now, returning to the state of a desperate person turning to any doctor.

However, what Fu Hongmei said made sense. Even if the doctor couldn't cure my grandmother, he could find a way to preserve her physical body for a bit longer.

"Can we let that doctor come back with me today?" My tone was somewhat impatient.

"It's already eight o'clock, and it's pitch black outside. The road is already hard to walk on with the heavy snow, and in this pitch-darkness, we wouldn't feel at ease letting you cross the river alone!" Fu Hongmei persuaded softly.

"Xiaolu, stay and sleep at home tonight. Wait until tomorrow morning when the snow lightens up a bit before leaving; it's not like waiting one more night matters."

Fu Hongmei reminded me. With night falling, I definitely wouldn't dare go near the riverbank again.

Yet if I took that mountain path again on the return trip, wouldn't I end up face-to-face with the paper doll elder sister once more?

Thinking of this, a chill wracked my entire body.

So be it. It's safer to make do for a night at the Wen family and leave when dawn breaks.

After all, I am supposedly their biological daughter; surely they wouldn't haul me off to northern Myanmar to harvest my kidneys while I was asleep!

When Wen Youcai and the others heard that I was willing to stay overnight, the joy on their faces couldn't be faked, showing they genuinely wanted me to stay.

At dinner, Fu Hongmei prepared a total of ten dishes, chicken, duck, fish, beef, mutton, and seafood, even more lavish than a New Year's Eve dinner.

In the center of the table sat a steamed King Crab. Although it had been frozen and the texture wasn't all that astonishing, it was enough to make me sigh inwardly.

It seemed the Wen family was truly wealthy, and much more low-profile than the village chief's family. I wondered what kind of business they ran.

Wen Youcai and Fu Hongmei kept serving food onto my plate, and within a short while, the food in my bowl was piled high.

Before I could finish what was in my bowl, Fu Hongmei placed a crab leg into it as well, but Wen Ting was obviously displeased and slammed her chopsticks heavily onto the table.

"Mom, didn't you say this King Crab was bought for me?"

Wen Youcai didn't care. While dishing out soup for me, he brushed it off, "You couldn't finish it all by yourself anyway. What's wrong with giving your older sister a crab leg? I'll buy you another one later!"

Wen Ting was so angry her eye rims turned red, and she bit her lip, yelling, "Mom, Dad, you're biased!"

With that, she turned and headed upstairs, returning to her own bedroom, and slammed the door shut with a loud *bang*.

Fu Hongmei looked somewhat embarrassed. "This child Wen Ting has been spoiled by us. Don't take it to heart, Xiaolu!"

I raised an eyebrow, said nothing, and gnawed that crab leg completely clean.

After dinner, Fu Hongmei led me upstairs to rest.

"The guest room hasn't been lived in for a long time, and there's a lot of dust. Tonight, you can sleep with Xiaotang. It'll be a good chance for you sisters to get to know each other and bond."

Before I could open my mouth to refuse, Fu Hongmei pushed open Wen Ting's bedroom door.

Pink background walls, a cloud-shaped chandelier, a European-style vanity, and a draped bed that looked extremely soft.

A girl living here would practically be an escaped Disney princess, satisfying every young girl's fantasy.

Yet Wen Ting blocked the bedroom door with her body, cutting off my view as well.

She glared at me fiercely and said angrily, "I have no bond with her! She can sleep wherever she wants, but she is not allowed into my room!"

Fu Hongmei scolded her, "Xiaotang, don't be willful. Lin Jianlu is your older sister!"

"I don't have an older sister!" Wen Ting's attitude was extremely disdainful. "You guys acknowledge her, but I certainly don't!"

"Just as well, I don't want to share a room with you either; your perfume gives me a headache." I spoke indifferently.

Fu Hongmei was momentarily put in a difficult position and hesitated. "Then... Xiaolu, would you mind sleeping with Mom tonight?"

I gave a noncommittal response.

When I was waiting for trains to go home from school, to save half a night's hotel fee, I had even slept on plastic chairs; I had nothing to be picky about.

Wen Ting looked as though she still wanted to say something, but Fu Hongmei stopped her with a look.

I followed Fu Hongmei into her bedroom, and she dug out a clean set of pajamas and handed them to me.

The clothes emitted a faint scent of camellia, just like the smell of her hair, warm and understated.

With the lights turned off, Fu Hongmei and I lay flat on that large, soft bed, with enough space in the middle for another person to sleep.

In the darkness, I secretly glanced at her profile, thinking that blood ties are truly terrifying.

The woman in front of me had abandoned me, and we hadn't seen each other in twenty years, yet deep down, I still wanted to be close to her.

Perhaps choosing to stay overnight tonight was a mistake; they made me experience the feeling of being cherished by parents.

Much like a long-parched traveler drinking sweet spring water, I unconsciously wanted to obtain more.

I even felt a bit jealous of Wen Ting; what I couldn't get, she had already enjoyed for twenty years.

That was why I had eaten that crab leg, just like I was trying to compete with Wen Ting.

Only the sound of my breathing and Fu Hongmei's remained in the room, and I knew she definitely wasn't asleep either.

"Xiaolu, would you like Mom to hold you while you sleep?" Fu Hongmei broke the silence first, her low, soft tone sounding exceptionally gentle in the dark.

I turned around, facing away from her.

Fu Hongmei didn't force the issue further, saying softly, "If you agree to acknowledge your father and mother, once Xiaotang goes abroad to study, her bedroom will be left for you. After that, our family will never be separated again."

I didn't answer, but I knew my heart was wavering.

Because they had precisely hit my desire for familial affection...

***

chapters.title: Gold in the Sand
chapters.content:
Hearing this, my heart felt as though it had been filled with cold lead, dragging me straight down.

What parental affection? It was all fake!

So they brought me back just to make me marry the Dragon King in place of Wen Ting?

"The auspicious hour has arrived, respectfully inviting the Dragon King to receive his bride..." Wen Youcai shouted loudly, kneeling toward the shrine directly ahead.

Only then did I see clearly that what was enshrined in the shrine was a dragon-headed, human-bodied statue carved from black sandalwood.

Beside the Dragon King's statue stood a memorial tablet, with striking vermilion brushstrokes spelling out none other than my own Eight Characters of birth!

I was so terrified I couldn't breathe, and turning around, I bolted for the door.

The Wen family seemed to hear my footsteps and quickly conversed, "Oh no, that girl found out!"

"Quick... quickly catch her, absolutely don't let her run away!"

I stepped barefoot into the snow, no longer caring about the cold, and ran for my life toward the village entrance.

"Xiaolu, where are you going? It's cold outside, come back quickly!" Fu Hongmei's feigned voice rang out behind me.

My mind was in utter chaos, with only a single thought filling my head: I must not be dragged back by them!

No starlight pierced the bitter, dark night.

Something was surging on the mountain, making rustling sounds, rushing down from the forest in a vague torrent.

I thought it was an avalanche, but when those things surged forth like a tidal wave, someone shouted from behind.

"Snakes, there are snakes!"

"Ah... snakes are biting people!"

Screams rose and fell all around us, sounding exceptionally shrill in the deep night.

The lights in the village lit up one after another, instantly turning the place brightly lit.

I looked closely, and the writhing things on the ground were actually all snakes!

Those snakes were dark brown in color with grayish reticulated patterns on their backs, a unique local species of Ussuri pit viper, cold-resistant and extremely venomous.

I didn't know where so many snakes had come from. To the naked eye, they were a pitch-black mass, overlapping and intertwining as they rapidly slithered from the woods into the village.

It was as if tens of thousands of snakes from the entire Greater Khingan Mountains had been mobilized and gathered in Yelong Village!

Yet today was only the second day of the second lunar month; shouldn't these snakes be hibernating?

The second day of the second lunar month...

I suddenly recalled what Long Mingyuan had said: I had a destined calamity in my life and wouldn't survive the second day of the second lunar month of this year!

Was I really going to lose my life to snakes today?

The road out of the village was completely blocked by those snakes. The fences were densely coiled with black pit vipers, their dual pupils shooting cold light in the dark, darting out their bright red forked tongues at me.

I had no choice but to turn back and run.

Those snakes actually followed closely behind, chasing me all the way to the Wen family courtyard.

Seeing me voluntarily running back barefoot, the Wen family members were just about to show mocking smiles when they instantly saw the vast, dark sea of snakes behind me!

Their smiles completely froze at the corners of their mouths...

"Snakes, so many snakes!"

Wen Ting let out a piercing scream, terrifying herself into hugging her head and shrinking onto the sofa.

The snake pack had organized themselves to surround the Wen family, blocking the courtyard in three inner and three outer layers.

They made "hissing" sounds, darting out long forked tongues as they continuously squeezed into the courtyard.

Fu Hongmei asked in terror, "How can there be so many snakes?"

"They... they were sent by the Dragon King to receive the bride!" Wen Youcai forced himself to calm down, a sinister tone in his voice.

I turned back, catching his gaze just as a fierce, murderous look was revealed in the depths of his eyes.

Before I could react, those snakes had already crawled toward where Wen Ting was.

One black snake as thick as a bowl seemed to be their leader. It reached Wen Ting first, and amidst her bouts of screams, slithered up along her pajama pants, tightly coiling around her slender waist.

Its bright red forked tongue darted out, leaving a trail of transparent mucus on her cheek.

"Dad, save me, Dad!" Wen Ting's cries were heart-rending, tears and snot streaming together as her proper lady image completely vanished.

Fu Hongmei grabbed a kitchen knife and rushed forward recklessly, "Baby, Mom is coming to save you!"

As a result, those snakes surrounded Wen Ting in the center, launching a dangerous offensive against Fu Hongmei.

Seeing this, Wen Youcai immediately knelt down and kowtowed. "Grandpa snakes, Lin Jianlu is the bride Lord Dragon King wants to marry! You caught the wrong person!"

As he spoke, Wen Youcai pointed his hand at me, and the snakes all over the courtyard seemed to truly understand his words, turning their heads in unison to look at me along the direction he pointed.

Those pairs of gloomy green, icy pupils were enough to give me nightmares for half a year...

They abandoned the chase of Wen Ting and rapidly attacked me.

I retreated desperately, already forced into a corner.

Those snakes bound my hands and feet like vines, their cool, smooth scales rubbing back and forth against my skin, making my hair stand on end.

I wanted to cry out for help, but when a person is terrified to the extreme, they lose their voice and can only produce rapid gasps.

The snake that had previously coiled around Wen Ting's waist was now resting on my chest, tilting its huge snake head to stare fixedly at me, its gloomy green pupils carrying a hint of confusion, as if appraising merchandise.

It opened its bloody maw at me, revealing those teeth as sharp and hooked as fishhooks, and I nearly fainted from the fishy stench.

Just when I thought I was going to perish in the snake's maw, the black jade pendant in my bosom burst forth with a fierce golden light, illuminating both banks of the river and the wilderness mountains, instantly making the world as bright as day.

The snakes wrapped around my body were instantly blasted a dozen meters away by that light, and the rest were cut cleanly in half at the waist, leaving snake corpses all over the courtyard.

Everyone collapsed weakly onto the ground, covered from head to toe in foul, bloody gore, looking utterly wretched...

The village gradually returned to tranquility.

I struggled to stand up, only to find my head spinning violently and a faint stinging sensation on my hand.

Looking down, two bright red tooth marks had unexpectedly appeared on my slender wrist...

My vision darkened, and I lost consciousness.

***

chapters.title: Fire Under the Mountain
chapters.content:
When I woke up again, the sun was already setting west outside the window.

A dull ache came from the back of my head, and the bizarre and terrifying memories from before I lost consciousness surfaced before my eyes.

I tried to crawl up from the bed, but my whole body was numb, and my limbs completely refused to obey.

What kind of snake bit me? The venom was so strong...

Whether the wound truly hurt that much or the truth was just too hard to accept, a sour, stinging sensation welled up in my eyes, gradually blurring my vision.

Suddenly.

The room door was pushed open, and Wen Ting walked in slowly, her pretty face regaining its arrogance.

"Let me go!" I glared at her angrily. "What you're doing is illegal! I'm going to call the police!"

"Sister, what are you talking about? You were bitten by a snake! But don't be afraid, we've already let blood from your wound to treat it; you're not going to die!" Wen Ting acted as though she hadn't heard my threat, walking over to the table on her own to pour a glass of water.

"You must be thirsty after sleeping for so long, right?"

I licked my dry, cracked lower lips and said nothing, my gaze locked firmly on the glass of water in her hand.

From last night until now, I hadn't had a single drop of water; my throat felt like it was smoking.

Wen Ting walked over holding that cup of water, the corners of her mouth curling into a disdainful arc, and with a flick of her hand, she splashed the entire glass of cold water right onto my face.

*Splash...*

The icy temperature made my whole body shrink, my eyelashes damp with water droplets, and I said angrily, "Wen Ting, what are you going crazy for?"

Wen Ting sat down on the edge of my bed, looking at my drowned-rat appearance, and giggled, "Daring to yell at me like that, what kind of thing do you think you are? You really take yourself for my 'older sister'?"

I clenched my teeth tightly, still glaring at her coldly.

"Why are you looking at me like that?" Wen Ting curled her lips in scornful disdain. "Feels great to have family doting on you, right? Too bad, you don't deserve it!

They brought you back just to have you marry that Dragon King lying in the coffin in place of me to bring good luck. I'm the one they brought up personally, so of course they can't bear to see me suffer through this hardship, but you're different...

How does a country bumpkin like you look anything like Mom and Dad's daughter? You even delusionally thought of taking my place? Keep dreaming!"

Those ice-cold water droplets flowed down my collarbone into my neckline, chilling my heart through to the bone. The piece of black jade slipped out from my collar, spotted by Wen Ting's sharp eyes.

"What is this thing?" she asked in surprise.

"Just a worthless piece of jade," I evaded her gaze.

"I saw it all! Was it this thing you used to kill those snakes back then?"

Filled with curiosity, Wen Ting reached out and touched the black jade pendant hanging in front of my chest. "I didn't expect that with all your rustic poverty, you'd have such a powerful treasure! This thing feels ice-cold to the touch; it looks like jade, yet it isn't jade. What material is it actually made of?"

"Don't touch it, or I'll make it kill you too!" I deliberately threatened her.

Wen Ting was indeed somewhat intimidated, immediately letting go and retreating behind the bed.

For a long time, the room remained dead silent, yet nothing happened at all.

I didn't know why Wen Ting was able to touch the black jade. Perhaps because our Eight Characters and blood ties were similar, the black jade mistook her for me and therefore did nothing to her.

Toyed with like this by me, Wen Ting was gnashing her teeth in anger. She snatched the black jade right off my neck, saying, "Country bumpkin, hand it over!"

"Give it back to me!" I grew even more furious, shouting sternly.

"It belongs to me now!" She casually played with that piece of black jade, shaking her head triumphantly.

The door opened once more, and Fu Hongmei walked in carrying a red sandalwood box, frowning at the sight. "Wen Ting, stop fooling around!"

Wen Ting gave a cold snort, and begrudgingly tucked the black jade into her own pocket.

Fu Hongmei opened that box, and inside lay a shockingly gorgeous red bridal gown, complete with everything from embroidered shoes and double-happiness headscarves to phoenix coronets and flowing robes.

"Xiaolu, look how luxurious the bridal gown Lord Dragon King sent is!" Fu Hongmei gently stroked the embroidery of dragons and phoenixes dancing auspiciously, reciting softly, "Just the pearls on these buttons are worth hundreds of thousands! When you marry over there, he certainly won't mistreat you!"

Startled by her words, I stared in terror at the red bridal gown in her hand, my voice turning hoarse of its own accord. "What do you mean?"

Fu Hongmei's expression remained calm as she slowly spoke, "The year I first became pregnant with you two sisters, I had a very strange dream. I dreamt that a huge black snake crawled out from the woods behind the village.

It told me I was pregnant with twins, and both were daughters.

If I was willing to hand over one of the daughters as a sacrifice to the Dragon King, Lord Dragon King would bless our family with wealth and honor from then on, making us the richest family in the entire county!

If I refused, our whole family would starve to death!"

Hearing this, I furrowed my brow deeply, gritting my teeth as I asked, "That was just a dream! For the sake of such an illusory dream, you threw me away?"

chapters.title: Pingdimu (Plane-Tree Wood)
chapters.content:
The look Fu Hongmei gave me no longer held joy or maternal affection, only indifference. "I thought it was just a nightmare at first, so I didn't pay it any mind.

It wasn't until I was eight months pregnant that your father and I were both laid off at the same time. The doctor checked and confirmed I was carrying twins, and both were girls!

True enough, our family soon became dirt poor. Even the money for my Caesarean section had to be borrowed from the neighbors.

The adults often went from one meal to the next without knowing where the next would come from. My milk supply was low; after feeding you, Xiaoting could only go hungry.

At night, too hungry to sleep, I would hold you two sisters and cry together.

Your father went and sold his blood twice, trading the money for a bit of cornmeal. He boiled a huge pot of watery porridge, which finally filled our stomachs.

Misfortunes never come singly. When you were three months old, you had your first sudden asthma attack, but the family truly had no money left to spare.

At that time, your father suggested: why not do what that big snake said and sacrifice you to the Dragon King? Perhaps our whole family could survive then!

That winter was so cold, the river was frozen with a thick layer of ice.

Your father carried you deep into the woods, believing you would freeze to death within a few hours, so he ran off after leaving you behind.

That night, I dreamed of that big snake again. It was coiled atop a rosewood chest, saying that inside were betrothal gifts for its daughter.

When I woke up, I hurriedly told your father to look outside the door. Sure enough, a large chest had inexplicably appeared in the courtyard.

Inside the chest, besides this set of red bridal robes, there were many valuable pieces of jewelry.

Your father and I were both overjoyed. Had we known that abandoning you would earn us such a huge sum of money, we wouldn't have had to suffer these past three months!

And strangely enough, ever since we abandoned you, our family's situation really did get better day by day!

Your father sold all that jewelry, and with that money, we played the stock market, bought real estate, and did business, never once taking a loss.

Six years later, we wanted to move away from this ghost of a place, go to Harbin to buy a big villa, and live the good life!

But on the very night we decided to move, that snake came again...

It looked exactly like the one that was sprawled across your chest last night. It also sprawled across Xiaoting's bed, flicking its forked tongue and saying we lacked integrity, asking why, since we had agreed to the Dragon King's marriage proposal back then, we were now going back on our word?

It bared its fangs at Xiaoting. I hurriedly fell to my knees and kowtowed, begging it and the Dragon King to forgive us.

Only then did that snake leave through the window, saying that on the second day of the second lunar month of the next Year of the Dragon, it would come to take my daughter away to bring good fortune to the Dragon King!

If I had any further thoughts of backing out, it would bite us to death and make us be buried along with the Dragon King!

What the snake said felt a bit strange to me. Weren't you already sacrificed to the Dragon King? Why was it still coming after my Xiaoting?

It was then that we found out you hadn't died, but had been picked up by Granny Lin on the other side of the river!"

Hearing this, I shivered all over. I had originally thought that their abandoning me back then was beyond their control, and I had even felt conflicted, tormented, and remorseful over it.

Little did I expect that they had gladly used me in exchange for wealth and glory, and even resented why I hadn't just died back then!

Fu Hongmei seemed to feel that since her true face was exposed, there was nothing left to hide, and she continued, "Over the years, we went to find your grandmother three times in total. She seemed to have foreseen that our purpose in wanting you back wasn't pure, and refused to agree to let us bring you back, no matter what.

She even tried to threaten us, saying that if we kept pestering you, she would cast witchcraft on us and let the gods punish us for the sins we had committed!

Before Lin Guixiang fell ill, it was hard enough just getting close to you.

But we neither had the heart to let Xiaoting marry the Dragon King, nor did we want to go back to the bitter days of not knowing where our next meal was coming from, so we could only stay here and wait for the right moment.

It wasn't until late last year that Xiaoting was admitted to a prestigious foreign university, and we wanted to send her abroad to study after the new year.

As a result, starting from New Year's Eve, the heavy snow fell without stopping. People inside couldn't get out, and people outside couldn't get in, as if this side of the mountains had been completely cut off from the mortal world.

We understood then that this was the Dragon King casting spells. Only when the wedding proceeded as scheduled on the second day of the second lunar month would he let us leave..."

After Fu Hongmei finished speaking, my heart felt hollow for a long time.

So Long Mingze hadn't lied to me. It really was my biological parents who had sold me to him!

"So your wanting to recognize me as your daughter was fake, and the affection and warmth you showed me were all fake, just to make me take Wen Ting's place in marrying the Dragon King and bringing him good fortune?"

A fine, dense pain tortured me like death by a thousand cuts, and I screamed hysterically, "But I am your daughter too! Wen Ting is your biological daughter, am I not one as well?"

"You are not!"

Fu Hongmei's expression suddenly changed, her tone turning shrill. "My only daughter is Xiaoting. How could a freak like you be my daughter!

Lin Guixiang said that you are the reincarnation of the deer spirit, and merely happened to borrow my belly to be born.

My biggest regret is that I didn't harden my heart and strangle you to death with my own hands back then! Then the Dragon King wouldn't have kept hounding us!

Our family wouldn't have lived in poverty, nor would we have been forced to stay in this godforsaken place..."

My tears choked in my throat, turning into a sneer.

When I was little, I saw that other kids all had parents, and only I didn't.

When I ran to ask Granny, she said I was an orphan and my parents were already dead.

I was upset about it for a long time, and even secretly made a wish to the gods, praying just to see my parents one more time, even if it was just to know what they looked like!

And right now, my biological mother was standing in front of me, telling me why she hadn't hardened her heart to strangle me to death...

She picked up that bright red bridal robe, walked toward me step by step, and said expressionlessly, "Put it on. Tonight, you're marrying over there."

***

chapters.title: Bishangtu (Wall Earth)
chapters.content:
"Take that thing away. Whoever wants to wear it can wear it, I'm not going to wear it!" I tried to struggle, but my whole body was numb, and my hands and feet simply wouldn't obey.

Wen Ting ruthlessly stomped her foot down on the back of my hand, sneering, "That's not up to you!"

She ripped open my sweater with a yank, grabbed the red bridal robe, and pulled it over my head.

"Get away, don't touch me!" I turned my head aside and bit down hard on her arm.

"Ah!" Wen Ting jumped in pain. "Mom, she bit me!"

"Xiaoting!" Fu Hongmei was frantic with worry. She beat at me while pulling Wen Ting backward, her eyes full of heartache.

Yet the more she did that, the harder I bit, as if pouring all my hatred into my teeth.

If there were a mirror now, I would find my eyes bloodshot, with a ferocious expression more terrifying than a starving wolf.

Hearing the commotion, Wen Youcai burst in. Seeing the three of us tangled together, he slapped me hard across the face.

The blow left my head spinning, a fishy, salty taste rising in my mouth, and I nearly lost consciousness again.

Wen Ting didn't dare get close to me anymore, shrinking into a corner and sobbing miserably. Her jade-like arm was bitten until it bled, the tooth marks deeply branded into her flesh, a brand that would probably never fade for the rest of her life.

Fu Hongmei bandaged Wen Ting, her heart aching terribly at the depth of the wound as she glared at me with hatred. "Lin Guixiang was right. You're nothing but a debt-collecting ghost, a cursed lone star; nothing good ever comes to anyone who gets close to you! You brought ruin upon our family, now you've caused Lin Guixiang's death, and now you want to bring disaster to Xiaoting, right?"

I shook my head unconsciously, unable to put my overflowing grievance into words.

"Dad, hurry up and marry her off to the Dragon King. I don't want to see her anymore!" Wen Ting cried, clutching her wound.

Wen Youcai walked over to me and said darkly, "Don't blame us for being cruel. If you want to blame someone, blame your own bad luck for catching the Dragon King's eye! Only when you marry the Dragon King will the snow outside stop. Do you expect the people of two villages to be buried along with you?"

Because my emotions were too intense, the unexpelled toxins in my body flared up again. I mumbled drowsily, "Don't come over... stay away from me..."

In my vision, Wen Youcai had already split into double images. The last bit of consciousness I held onto was the sound of their ruthless dialogue.

"The snake that came to welcome the bride was killed by this baneful star. What should we do now?"

"We can't miss the auspicious hour, or the whole family will suffer! Hurry up and put the bridal robe on her, let's take her to the Dragon King Temple ourselves..."

***

I woke up with a start, my throat burning as if I had swallowed a knife. Opening my heavy eyelids, I was met with pitch-black darkness.

Yet my hands and feet could finally move; it seemed the toxicity had worn off.

I propped myself up, wanting to sit up, but my head banged heavily against the wooden board above, making me gasp in pain and realizing something was wrong.

Whose house would be built so small that a person couldn't even stand up?

Unless... it was a coffin?

Could it be that I was already dead?

The thought gave me a genuine fright, and I instinctively reached out to feel around my surroundings, only to brush against cold, elastic flesh.

A slender man was actually lying right beside me!

What the hell? Was this a joint burial tomb?

"Stop moving around!"

That crisp voice carried a hint of displeasure, yet sounded exceptionally familiar.

"Long Mingyuan... is that you?" I asked tentatively.

After a moment, I heard his low response. "Mn."

This inexplicably familiar scene reminded me of the erotic dreams that had played out every night prior.

Long Mingyuan, lying beside me, seemed to guess what I was thinking and said indifferently, "This isn't a dream."

"Not a dream? Then why am I in a coffin..."

I paused mid-sentence as the scenes from before I lost consciousness flooded back into my mind.

It was Wen Youcai and Fu Hongmei who had carried me to the Dragon King Temple, forcibly pressing me to kowtow three times to the Dragon King's statue until my forehead was split open.

They had also pried open my mouth and forced down a cup of bitter nuptial wine.

Finally, they placed an unresponsive me inside the Dragon-Suppressing Coffin and closed the lid...

My heart was filled with both panic and confusion as I asked, "But shouldn't the person getting married to me be Long Mingze? Why has it become you?"

Long Mingyuan remained silent, but I distinctly sensed the air pressure drop by several degrees.

Actually, from the moment I first saw him, a sense of inexplicable joy had welled up in my heart.

Coupled with the fact that the piece of black jade he gave me had saved my life several times before, my impression of him was not entirely bad.

Yet the oppressive aura he exuded made me somewhat fearful. It seemed... he really didn't want to see me.

Hence, I began to scramble outward using both hands and feet.

Regrettably, the space inside was far too cramped, and the four walls were much too damp and smooth. I tumbled right onto Long Mingyuan's body, my forehead brushing against a trace of cool softness.

"Mmph..."

The two of us groaned simultaneously.

Fresh blood welled up from the wound on my brow once more, a sweet and fishy scent diffusing into the thin air.

"I said, don't move anymore!" Long Mingyuan commanded in a low voice, sounding as though he were suppressing something.

"I... I'm sorry!" The earlier commotion had brought me even closer to him, pressing almost my entire body against his. This was my first time in reality having such close physical contact with a male.

His heavy breathing filled my ears, laced with a dangerous undertone.

I hadn't even moved...

Was he really trying to consummate the marriage with me?

"Long Mingyuan, stop this!" I reached out to push him away, only to have my wrists seized and pinned above my head.

The breath Long Mingyuan blew against my ear grew progressively heavier, his voice laced with suppressed anger. "I told you to stay away from the Dragon King Temple, and even more so not to touch this Dragon-Suppressing Coffin. Why wouldn't you listen?"

Big Brother, I didn't want to either! The Wen family forcibly shoved me in!

I felt his teeth lightly graze the side of my neck, sending a shudder through my whole body and terrifying me so much that my voice carried a sob. "I know I was wrong, won't you let me go?"

"Too late!" Long Mingyuan's voice was cruelly devoid of a shred of warmth. "Just now, I touched the wound on your brow. Your blood contains the components of a deer spirit. A dragon's nature is inherently lustful; deer blood is a potent aphrodisiac to our dragon clan..."

His words made me want to cry without tears. God damn it, a potent aphrodisiac!

"You have to control yourself!" I squeezed my eyes shut in despair.

His cold, clinging kisses traveled all the way down from my neck as he said with strained endurance, "Forgive me, I didn't want to touch you..."

The elaborate bridal robes on my body were violently torn apart, the sound of ripping fabric echoing within the narrow confines of the coffin, *Rip...*

Through the small gap I had just knocked open, light illuminated his exquisite, ink-painting-like brows and eyes, also letting me clearly see the deep, restrained desire at the bottom of his gaze.

The hem of my skirt was lifted at some point, and a cold breeze swept across the curves of my legs, making me tremble uncontrollably.

The man above me was both so familiar and so strange. My nasal cavity was filled with his unique dragon-saliva fragrance, mixed with the sweet, sticky scent of blood.

The tragic part was that I discovered my own body was growing feverish.

That cup of nuptial wine had a problem.

chapters.title: Gilded Gold
chapters.content:
Though such things happened to me every single night, after all, a spring dream was still just a dream.

Even if it felt very real, it lacked a great deal of physical sensation.

When I knew there was no escaping this ordeal no matter what, I had no choice but to forcefully brainwash myself.

It's okay, it's okay, it'll be over soon...

This kiss was just like the man himself, cold and restrained, yet carrying an overwhelming sense of aggression.

Perhaps due to the effect of that nuptial wine, my consciousness gradually drifted away.

I was like a fish seemingly out of water, my whole body limp inside the coffin, panting heavily for the thin air.

That hoarse voice rolled out from his throat, sounding utterly merciless as it fell against my ear: "Dragon mating takes as short as three days and three nights, or as long as a year and a half. This has only just begun..."

A year and a half? Why don't you talk about five years of the college entrance examination and three years of mock tests instead!

I cried out in a breakdown, "Why don't you just kill me instead!"

In a daze, I seemed to hear a low chuckle, so magnetic and pleasant: "I advise you to save your strength."

These three days and three nights, I had no idea how I had survived them.

Unconsciousness took up the majority of the time, and every time I opened my eyes, I could see that cinnabar mole between his brows swaying gently.

Before losing consciousness entirely, I saw him gently kissing my fingers, his gaze pious and persistent, as if hiding an indescribable emotion, sighing: "In this lifetime, I will surely protect you well and never let you meet that kind of end again..."

I desperately wanted to ask him, what kind of end?

But my eyelids felt as heavy as a thousand catties, my head drooped to one side, and I plunged into a lengthy dream.

***

"Xiaolu, wake up quickly!"

"Xiaolu, stop sleeping, wake up right now!"

This voice was somewhat familiar, it seemed to be... Granny!

Granny, is that you?

I snapped my eyes open, only to find myself still lying inside that Dragon-Suppressing Coffin, and outside, the day was already bright.

The coffin lid had been violently split in half and lay horizontally on the ground, while the person who had been beside me was long gone.

Rubbing my dizzy head, I sat up from the coffin and looked around blankly, but the temple was empty.

In my dream, I clearly heard Granny's voice, yet there was no sign of Granny here.

Only the solemn and dignified statue of the Dragon King above my head looked down at me with those merciless and desireless stone eyes.

The mere thought that I had actually done that kind of thing in front of the divine statue filled me with such shame and anger that I wished I could smash my head against this coffin and die.

My lower abdomen felt somewhat uncomfortably swollen, so I climbed out of the coffin with difficulty and picked up the torn pieces of clothing one by one.

At that moment, I caught sight of two deep red, petal-like marks on the hem of my skirt, and I instantly snapped to my senses.

Unlike previous dreams, this time I had truly broken my vow of chastity...

Oh no!

Granny had said before that my virgin blood would break the seal and release the evil flood dragon suppressed inside the coffin.

Yet now, not only had I lost my virginity, but I had also done that kind of thing with that evil flood dragon...

That destined tribulation in the end still hadn't been averted; was I really going to die?

An unknown fear washed over me. It turned out that the most terrifying thing was not death, but waiting to die.

I only prayed for the heavens to show mercy and allow me to retrieve Granny's soul before I died.

If I was destined to die, then please let me bring Granny back to life!

Thinking of Granny, I forced myself to pull it together, put on that tattered wedding dress, and walked out of the temple doors with arduous steps.

The continuous snow of an entire month had actually stopped, and the horizon showed faint signs of clearing. The villagers, who had been cooped up at home for a long time, also began to venture outside.

Everything was moving in a good direction; only I grew increasingly anxious and uneasy.

Passing by the Wen family's courtyard, Wen Ting was humming a song inside while sunning herself. That fierce dog barked wildly the moment it saw me.

"Woof, woof, woof..."

She turned her head and saw me, screaming as if she had seen a ghost, "Dad, that jinx is back again!"

Wen Ting turned to run, but I grabbed her by the collar and asked in a cold voice, "Where is that piece of black jade? Return it to me!"

Wen Youcai and Fu Hongmei ran out of the house, both looking startled when they saw me standing there safe and sound.

"How can this be? Weren't you already..."

"Already dead, right?" I laughed self-deprecatingly. "Too bad a jinx of the heavenly star isn't so easily killed. 'Misfortunes outlast a millennium', surely you've heard that saying?"

Wen Youcai was the head of the household after all, so he mustered up his courage and roared, "We've already disowned you, what are you coming back for?"

I grabbed Wen Ting by the collar and slammed her hard onto the ground. "She took my things, she has to return them! Otherwise, do you think I'd ever want to see you people again?"

Fu Hongmei helped Wen Ting up and asked with heartache, "Baby, did you hurt anywhere? Let mom take a look."

"Wen Ting, what did you take? Give it back to her quickly! Even things from a jinx you dare to take, aren't you afraid of bad luck?" Wen Youcai reprimed in a low voice.

Wen Ting bit her lip, glaring at me angrily, seemingly still unwilling to hand it over.

I deliberately intimidated her, "This black jade pendant was given to me by the one in the coffin. If you don't want to return it, that's fine too; I can have him come out personally and chat with you, how about that?"

As expected, Wen Ting's face showed fear. She stopped sobbing and threw the piece of black jade at me.

I caught it, having no desire to have any further involvement with them, and turned to walk away.

However, Wen Youcai squinted as he looked at the tattered red wedding dress on my body. "Wait, take off that outfit!"

I froze.

Fu Hongmei stepped forward and shoved him, asking uncomprehendingly, "What are you doing?"

"The pearls on those clothes are worth quite a bit of money, we can't just let her off so cheaply!" Wen Youcai muttered to her in a low voice.

I sneered coldly. Having lived this long, this was the first time I had ever seen such a shameless person!

Yet I ignored him and continued walking forward.

Wen Youcai, however, grabbed my arm and violently tore off half a sleeve!

My snow-white shoulder was bared to the biting cold wind, exposing bruised, deep purple tooth marks and lingering kiss marks.

Just looking at it was startling; one could only imagine how crazy those three days of romance had been.

Wen Ting's expression was one of disgust and terror, and she turned her head away along with Fu Hongmei.

Yet Wen Youcai still tried to reach out and strip my clothes off. Anger flared up inside me instantly, and using the piece of black jade in my palm as a weapon, I slashed a gash across his wrist. "Get lost, don't touch me!"

A faint red light shot out from the edge of the black jade, and Wen Youcai's right hand was cleanly severed right from the wrist bone, dropping into the snow as blood instantly gushed forth like a fountain.

chapters.title: Covered Lamp Fire
chapters.content:
None of us had reacted yet, Wen Youcai included.

He first looked at his wrist, spurting blood without stopping, then at his right hand lying on the ground, its fingers still curling faintly, the nerves still at work.

After a long moment, Wen Youcai let out a heart-rending scream. "Ahhh!"

"My hand!"

I gripped the blood-stained piece of black jade tightly, unable to believe I had done this.

I had only swiped it lightly, without using much force at all. How could Wen Youcai's hand have come off?

I had underestimated this piece of black jade. It could obviously cut through iron like mud, and I had been using it to open packages...

What a terrible waste of a treasure!

Wen Youcai was still kneeling there wailing. Fu Hongmei hurriedly took off her coat and wrapped it around his bleeding wound.

"Quick, call an ambulance!" Fu Hongmei shrieked at Wen Ting, who was frozen with fright.

While they were in an uproar and no one was stopping me anymore, I quietly slipped out.

Wen Youcai's hand probably couldn't be reattached. The snow had stopped, but the thick snow on the roads hadn't melted, so an ambulance still couldn't get through.

Thinking of this, I felt no guilt or pity at all. If anything, I felt relieved.

So what if they were my birth parents? They gave birth to me and never raised me, and then treated me as a sacrifice to trade for wealth and status.

After all the cruel things they did to me, I had only cut off Wen Youcai's right hand. That wasn't excessive, was it?

Crossing the river, I returned to Dragon-Guarding Village.

The wedding gown was thin as gauze and torn to shreds, and I was so cold I was nearly numb.

By the roadside a few children pointed at me and asked, "Mom, is she the bride the Dragon King married?"

I turned my head and saw that the villagers who used to live in harmony with me were all looking at me with strange eyes.

The village was too small to hide secrets.

The news that I had been married off to the Dragon King to bring good luck had already traveled from the far bank to Dragon-Guarding Village.

The endless snow, the road through the mountains cut off, the village chief's stillborn child, and Granny suddenly falling from the stage...

All these strange and eerie events seemed to have become omens of "the Dragon King taking a wife."

Now that I was wearing a wedding gown and had crawled out of the Dragon-Suppressing Coffin, the villagers were even more convinced that all of this had something to do with me, and avoided me as if I were a plague god.

They stood far off by the roadside, pulling their own children back so they wouldn't come near me.

I gathered the half a sleeve left on my shoulder, gave them a cold look, endured those stares of fear or contempt, and kept walking toward home.

From the crowd, Aunt Wang's plump figure pushed toward me. "Xiaolu, where have you been these days?"

"Aunt Wang..." The moment I opened my mouth, I almost cried.

Aunt Wang took off her army coat and wrapped it around my body, marked with bruises. She hugged me with heartache, her voice choked. "You child, how did you get yourself into this state!"

I pressed my lips together and asked quietly, "I'm fine. How is my grandmother?"

Aunt Wang avoided my eyes, and her tone turned heavy. "Your grandmother... she's gone!"

It felt as though I had been struck hard by a bronze bell, and a deafening roar filled my ears. Even my breathing stopped for a moment.

"How could this happen..." I murmured.

"Last night your grandmother called out a few times, 'Xiaolu, wake up,' and then she stopped breathing, and her heart stopped too... If you had come back sooner, maybe you could have seen her one last time!" There was unconcealed blame in Aunt Wang's words.

I clutched my chest and stumbled toward home, crying out, "Granny!"

So the voice I had heard from inside the coffin wasn't an illusion after all. It was her dying call.

She had woken me, and she herself had fallen asleep forever.

I threw myself down beside Granny's bed and took her already cold hand, trying to warm her with the heat of my face, only to find I was as frozen as a block of ice myself.

Granny lay there peacefully, her white pupils closed, as if she were only sleeping.

I couldn't believe she was really dead. In my memory she was a shaman everyone revered, always calm and composed, protected by the gods. How could she die so easily?

"Xiaolu, your grandmother was seventy-four this year. Seventy is rare from ancient times, and around here that counts as a long life. Don't be too sad, and try to bear it," Aunt Wang sighed, wiping tears from the corners of her eyes.

Aunt Wang's words reminded me that however powerful a shaman is, she is still flesh and blood. They are human.

And humans grow old, fall ill, and die.

Granny had already been in divine concealment for half a month. I had refused to believe it and treated it as an illness to avoid facing.

But Granny was gone. What was the point of my crawling back from that coffin, barely alive?

"Xiaolu, were you at your birth parents' place these days?" Aunt Wang looked at my ruined state and hesitated to speak. "Judging by this, they didn't treat you well. Even now that your grandmother is gone, you shouldn't go back there."

I closed my eyes in grief, my heart full of regret.

The family love I had longed for so long had been right beside me all along. I had blindly chased blood ties and overlooked the person in this world who was best to me.

My once-clouded heart had finally awakened, but it was too late.
