Aunt Wang comforted me a few more times. Seeing that I was too dazed to take in anything, she went home to cook for her son.

I nestled beside Granny's bed, curled up next to her like I had when I was little, but Granny would never tell me stories again.

My mind was a blank. I didn't know what else I could do, and I even secretly hoped the calamity fated for me would come sooner, so that I could die together with Granny and perhaps meet her on the road to the Yellow Springs.

My eyes were sore and swollen from crying, and I drifted into a daze and fell asleep.

In the dead of night, a cold wind blew open the half-closed door.

The bone-piercing chill made my whole body shudder, and in a haze I caught sight of a figure standing in our yard.

I walked out of the room and saw a tall, slender white figure standing under the tree. I couldn't tell what the fabric was made of, but from a distance it gleamed like silver poured down from the moon.

He turned to face me, and silver hair drifted lightly across his handsome face.

His emerald eyes, like cold stars in the midnight sky, were full of arrogance and disdain, and a wicked smile curled his lips. "My Consort, why don't you say anything when you see your husband? Are you so happy you've gone silly?"

I asked in shock, "Long Mingze, why are you here?"

"Who allowed you to address me by name? Since we've already bowed to heaven and earth, you should call me husband!" Long Mingze said teasingly.

When he came closer and saw my red, swollen eyes from crying, his tone was full of disgust. "Tsk, why are you crying like this? How ugly!"

I stepped back warily. "First explain clearly why the person who consummated the marriage with me was Long Mingyuan?"

chapters.title: Heavenly River Water
chapters.content:
Long Mingze wore a look of utter indifference, his hands clasped behind his back as he said lazily, "You want to ask about this? Well, that's a long story."

I gritted my teeth. "Then make it short!"

A trace of impatience flashed across the corners of his lips. "Haven't you already guessed the relationship between Long Mingyuan and me? Long Mingyuan and I are twins. He was born two hours before me, and I was forced to call him older brother.

That year, during his ascension ritual, he suffered a deviation in his practice, fell into the evil path, and turned into a wicked flood dragon.

Later, he brought disaster to the world, making life unbearable for the people on both banks, so I acted on behalf of heaven and defeated him.

I was also severely injured, and my soul was damaged. Left with no other choice, I had to share a single soul with him.

He was sealed inside the Dragon Suppressing Coffin, while I slumbered at the bottom of the Heilongjiang River. And so it has been for a full thousand years."

My mind couldn't process this for a moment, and I was utterly bewildered. "The two of you share a single soul? That means... you're actually the same person? Ah, no... the same dragon?"

Long Mingze seemed angered by my words. A gloomy aura radiated from his entire body, and his eyes were filled with disdain. "I am me, and he is he! Don't compare me to that maggot!"

That made me even more confused. Since they were two independent individuals, why did they both come after me?

"As for this matter, I did indeed keep it from you." Long Mingze shot me a sideways glance, his look resembling one cast at a lowly ant. "Long Mingyuan and I now share a single soul. Only by first breaking his seal can I be awakened from my slumber.

So I had no choice but to wrong you and have you consummate the marriage with him!"

I simply couldn't believe my ears. What kind of bizarre event was this? The younger brother married me, but let the older brother consummate the marriage with me?

"Do your dragon clans practice polyandry? Or do you have some special fetish, enjoying cuckolding each other?" I was so angry I didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

Was the dragon clan so dirt poor they couldn't afford anything? To marry a wife and only be able to cough up a single bride price?

I knew that in remote mountain areas in the past, there used to be such uncivilized customs where brothers would share a wife to save money.

Back then, as a casual onlooker reading such news, I would sigh and say, "Those cunning, poor men!"

Now that the drama had come home to my own courtyard and I had become the protagonist, my worldview was shattered into pieces so fine they couldn't even be glued back together.

"What about Long Mingyuan? Where is he?" I asked, suppressing my anger.

"Is Long Mingyuan's bed performance really that good, making you so unforgettable of him?" Long Mingze's lips turned down in displeasure. "However, he has no time to see you right now. I advise you not to set your heart on him!"

Seeing that his words carried a deeper meaning, I was just about to question him clearly when he raised his hand and reached for my tear-swollen eyes.

"Although you have lost your purity, I won't despise you. From now on, you will still be my Dragon King Consort. As long as you obediently listen to me, I will treat you well!"

"Don't touch me!"

I forcefully slapped his hand away. Humiliation and anger made my entire body tremble, and I held back the impulse to curse him out loud. "What do you take me for? A plaything for you two brothers to trample on as you please? Even if my parents sold me to you, I don't owe you anything!

Since you've already woken up, from now on, we each take our own path. You go back to being your great Dragon King who saves the world, and we'll be even!"

Long Mingze's gaze suddenly turned gloomy, his jaw tightening, clearly provoked into anger.

With a grab of his hand, I felt my body stop obeying me once more. I actually walked toward him of my own accord and was fiercely seized by the neck.

"Ungrateful wretch! You have already bowed before the Dragon King's statue, drank the nuptial wine, and even consummated the marriage. From birth to death, you belong to the Dragon King! Unless you die, don't even dream of escaping!"

"If you want to kill me, go ahead and do it. Don't think about bullying me anymore!" I was on the verge of suffocation, and involuntary tears slipped down my face.

Long Mingze furrowed his brow, his expression a mix of irritation and impatience. "Women are truly troublesome! Stop crying, who said I was going to kill you?"

"Then get the hell out of my house! I don't want to see you ever again!" I squeezed out through tight breaths.

Long Mingze's expression was extremely ugly. The hand grasping my neck tightened slightly as he gritted his teeth. "No one has ever dared to say that word to me. What kind of thing are you, daring to speak to me like this?"

He was choking me so I couldn't catch my breath, and just when I thought I was about to be choked to death by him, his outline dimmed slightly, and his body gradually turned transparent.

"I've only just recovered my true form, and my spiritual power is weak. The spiritual projection I manifested cannot be sustained for too long. I'll spare you this time, but in the future, you are not allowed to be so disrespectful to me!" Long Mingze narrowed his slender eyes and released his grip.

I finally came back to life, deep, thick oxygen filling my lungs as I coughed violently and incessantly.

"I won't be able to come see you often during this period. You can take this time to reflect on yourself. I'm not as patient as Long Mingyuan, pleasing me is the only thing you should be doing!" After saying that, Long Mingze's faint figure vanished into the courtyard.

Reflect on myself... and please him?

In his wildest dreams!

My heart was filled with anger and sorrow. I returned to Granny's bedside, rested my head on her arm, and cried, "Granny, what should I do?"

There was no response, only the howling of the biting cold wind filling the courtyard.

***

Early the next morning, Aunt Wang came over, bringing a lot of paper money and wreaths, along with a newly made burial shroud.

"Aunt Wang, what are you doing?" I asked.

"Xiaolu, Auntie knows you're grieving, but even though it's winter, we still need to clean up your grandmother's remains, don't we?"

Aunt Wang placed the items she brought by the door, rolled up her sleeves, and stepped forward. "Come on, give me a hand. Let's wipe your grandmother's body clean and put the shroud on her, so she can leave in peace!"

No matter how reluctant I was to accept it, I had to face reality.

I got up, splashed my face with cold water, and helped Aunt Wang dress Granny in her shroud.

"Your grandmother was a shaman. I don't know what the funeral customs of shamanism are, so I didn't dare order a coffin from anyone. What do you plan to do after the first seven days?" Aunt Wang asked softly while wiping Granny's arms with a clean towel.

"Granny said before that shamans are given tree burials and return to nature after death. We just need to find a few wooden boards to lay across two tall birch trees and place her on top," I slowly began, my voice hoarse from crying.

Aunt Wang nodded and sighed softly. "You two are orphans and widows, and there isn't even a man in the house. When the seventh day comes, I'll have my old man come over to help you."

I thanked Aunt Wang and watched her out the door.

The house had been decorated like a mourning hall. The wreaths brought by Aunt Wang were placed by the bed, and a large funeral character "奠" (Mourning) was pasted on the wall.

Granny lay on the bed wearing her black burial shroud. Aside from the rustling sound of the cold wind blowing the paper money, everything was peaceful.

I knelt beside the fire basin, burning paper money aimlessly, while Long Mingze's words from the previous night involuntarily echoed in my mind.

The thought that from now on I would have to endure Long Mingze's fickle temper, forced to please him until the day my life ended...

I wished I could bite my tongue right then and there and follow Granny!

But Granny certainly wouldn't approve. She was calling out to me with her dying breath, telling me to wake up; how could she bear to let me go down below to keep her company?

Yet, if I really had to spend a lifetime with Long Mingze, that would be worse than death!

If I truly had to choose between the two brothers, I'd choose Long Mingyuan.

***

chapters.title: Great Post Earth
chapters.content:
The light sound of leather shoes stepping on the ground came from outside, drawing closer.

I turned my head and saw a man in a suit and leather shoes walking in from outside the courtyard.

He looked to be about my age, his hair slicked back so shiny it looked like a calf had licked it, exuding an air of astuteness and vulgarity.

"Excuse me, can I help you?" I asked doubtfully.

The man grinned. "Xiaolu, don't you remember me? I'm your junior high seatmate, Wang Shuang!"

Wang Shuang?

Wasn't he the seatmate whom Granny had dragged to the Dragon King Temple, only to run a high fever afterward and miss the high school entrance exams?

I vaguely searched my memories for traces of him from back then and suddenly realized, "Oh, it's you!"

Wang Shuang smiled until his eyes narrowed into two small slits, adding a bit of a wretched air to his face. "Xiaolu, long time no see. I heard you got into a key university, that's amazing!"

Feeling a bit awkward, I smiled dryly. "How have you been lately?"

Wang Shuang took off his hat and casually dusted off the floating snow. "Not bad. After missing the entrance exam that year, I didn't study anymore and went to Guangdong with my parents to do business, made a little money.

This New Year, my maternal grandmother said she wasn't feeling well, and my mom wanted to bring us back to the village to check on her.

As a result, it snowed every day here, and all the buses were suspended. It only started clearing up yesterday.

My father had someone find a tractor to drop us off at the foot of the mountain, and we walked the remaining few kilometers of mountain road ourselves."

Hearing this, I didn't feel very comfortable, since Wang Shuang dropping out of school was somewhat related to Granny.

Instead, Wang Shuang waved his hand dismissively. "Bah, how long ago was that? Besides, I was never cut out for studying anyway. Even if I went to high school, I wouldn't have gotten into college. It's better to go out into society early. Look at me now, I've already bought a car and a house!"

I praised him, "You bought a car and a house at just twenty years old, that's really impressive!"

Wang Shuang winked at me. "Yeah, I came back this time with another purpose. Look at me now: I have a car, a house, and a few small shops. I just lack a female master of the house..."

I vaguely sensed what he was driving at, so I didn't take up his cue, playing the fool with a smile.

Seeing that I didn't take the bait, Wang Shuang cast his gaze past me to examine the mourning hall behind, and sighed softly. "Alas, I heard about Granny Lin's passing this morning. Don't be too sad. I'll be staying in the village for a while longer, so if you have any difficulties, just come find me."

Seeing that he didn't hold a grudge because of how Granny treated him back then, I secretly breathed a sigh of relief. "Thank you."

Wang Shuang suddenly grabbed my hand, rubbing his thumb back and forth across the back of my hand, his tone ambiguous. "Xiaolu, do you think if it weren't for your grandmother back then, the two of us would have been a couple by now?"

His action truly startled me. I quickly shook off his hand, my voice turning cold. "No! Even if Granny hadn't stopped us, we wouldn't have worked out, because I don't like you at all!"

Wang Shuang's shrewd triangular eyes narrowed slightly, looking somewhat sinister in the dim yellow candlelight. "Is that so? What a pity..."

He mentioned Granny, so I couldn't help asking a question that had troubled me for many years: "That day at the Dragon King Temple, what on earth did you see?"

Wang Shuang's expression suddenly froze, his facial muscles twitching. Stammering, he began to back toward the door. "I didn't see anything... I'm... I'm going back first. I'll come see you tonight!"

"Hey..."

I actually only wanted to ask Wang Shuang whether what he saw in the Dragon King Temple that night was Long Mingze or Long Mingyuan?

As a result, the moment I started to ask, Wang Shuang ran faster than a rabbit!

Thinking that I had poked at his psychological trauma and that he wouldn't come looking for me again, I was proven wrong.

That very night, he actually followed me into my bedroom...

***

The custom in our village was that when an elderly person passed away, their remains needed to be laid out for seven days before burial.

Because of Granny's special status and the widespread rumors about my marriage to the Dragon King, no one dared to come to offer condolences.

However, I still followed the rules and left the front door wide open to make it convenient for Granny's ghost to "return home."

I had too many things I hadn't yet said to Granny. Even if she was a ghost, being able to see her one more time would be enough!

At night, the white candle was blown out by the wind. I rubbed my dry, tear-sore eyes and got up to look for matches in the bedroom.

The moment I stepped into the room, before I even had time to turn on the light, a figure pulled me into an embrace, wrapping arms around my waist.

Thinking it was Long Mingze coming to torment me again, I struggled and shoved, only to touch a handful of stubble. I shrieked, "Ah, who are you?"

The man tightly hugged my waist, and while unbuttoning my clothes with his other hand, he pressed me down onto the kang. "Xiaolu, I've missed you to death all these years!

I've liked you since junior high. Back then, when you sat next to me as my seatmate, the skirts of our school uniforms were so short... every day a pair of fair legs would dangle in front of my eyes, and I wanted to touch you just like this back then!

But your grandmother wouldn't agree, and she even scared and threatened me...

Now that your grandmother is finally dead, no one is stopping us anymore. Let's be together!"

Recognizing that the man in front of me was Wang Shuang, I raised my hand and dealt him a fierce slap across the face. "Calm down! I said it before, I don't like you!"

Instead of getting angry after being slapped, Wang Shuang mumbled incoherently as he leaned toward my face. "You don't need to like me to do this, as long as it feels good!

Look, my name is Wang Shuang (Pleasure). Do it with me, and I can make you feel good to death!"

As he whispered those vulgar, unbridled words close to my ear, my stomach churned, and I kicked out desperately at his feet.

It was then I realized the vast difference in physical strength between a man and a woman. Even though I had used every ounce of my strength, he picked me up out of thin air as if lifting a chick and threw me onto the bed.

The back of my head struck the headboard with a heavy thud, and my vision was filled with white static.

Wang Shuang took off his jacket and puckered his lips to kiss me. I quickly turned my head to dodge, and happened to catch sight of the black jade resting on the cabinet.

I reached out to grab it, and just as my fingers brushed its edge, Wang Shuang grabbed my shoulders and tore away my mourning clothes.

The marks left by Long Mingyuan earlier had not yet faded, and the faint red prints and bruises were completely exposed to the air.

Wang Shuang narrowed his eyes, his expression a mix of anger and excitement as his breathing grew heavy. "So you really do have a man? All these marks... tsk tsk. I never expected that while you look so pure and chaste on the outside, you're actually such a slut in bed!"

A strong sense of humiliation gripped my heart. I bit my lower lip hard, clutching the piece of black jade in my palm.

Just as I was debating whether to cut off one of his arms or castrate him on the spot, a ball of black fog suddenly erupted inside the room.

The fog gradually took human form, and Long Mingze's snow-white robes appeared before me.

The corners of his lips curved upward in a mocking smirk. "Consort, would you call this... being caught in bed?"

chapters.title: Hairpin and Bracelet Gold
chapters.content:
"Did my brother fail to satisfy you, leaving you with the energy to sneak around here?" Long Mingze touched his chin and said with a click of his tongue, "You can even stomach someone who looks like this. You really are desperate!"

Wang Shuang looked up, thinking her man had returned, and was about to curse, but the moment he clearly saw Long Mingze, deep terror surfaced in his eyes.

"It's... it's you? You're the one I saw at the Dragon King Temple the other day!"

Hearing this, I looked at Long Mingze.

He stood lazily in the corner. Moonlight streamed through the window lattice, casting a glow upon his pleasing face. A wicked smile hung at the corners of his mouth, and his gaze was chilling.

"Now that you mention it, I do seem to recall a bit... I chopped off your little finger back then. It seems you haven't learned your lesson yet, daring to covet the Dragon King's woman!"

Only then did I notice that a section of Wang Shuang's right little finger was missing.

Wang Shuang's face flushed red, his body continuously shrinking into the corner, his lips trembling with fear, "No, don't come over..."

A sinister look stained the depths of Long Mingze's eyes. He raised a hand and made a grabbing motion, drawing Wang Shuang across the air toward him.

He seized Wang Shuang by the throat, hoisting him effortlessly into the air, and let out a cold snort, "I detest ungrateful humans like you the most. Since you're looking to die, I'll grant your wish!"

With that, the space between his fingers continued to tighten.

Wang Shuang struggled violently in the air like a dewatered fish, but to no avail. His pupils were forced wide, and his face turned a purplish-blue.

Immediately, a crisp snapping sound echoed in the room, and Wang Shuang went limp on the floor.

I was scared stupid by what had just happened.

Long Mingze had actually killed Wang Shuang right in front of me...

Seeing the look of astonishment and dull blankness on my face, Long Mingze said in disgust, "What's with that expression? Are you blaming me for interrupting your good time?"

I shifted my gaze away from Wang Shuang's corpse and asked Long Mingze with a gaping jaw, "Why did you kill him?"

Long Mingze wiped his hands indifferently, his tone still carrying a hint of slight arrogance, "He wanted to rape you. I helped you kill him, shouldn't you be thanking me?"

"I really am thanking you a lot, directly turning me into a murderer!" I squeezed these words out through my teeth.

Not understanding the meaning, Long Mingze tilted his head.

I took a deep breath and explained to him, "This is a society ruled by law. Killing people casually is a crime!"

The most terrifying part was that he had actually killed someone inside my house!

Long Mingze let out a scoffing, low hum, "So what if I killed someone? I am the Dragon King. Humans in my eyes are nothing more than ants; if I casually pinch a few to death, who would dare to convict me?"

I reached the limit of my patience, terrified and furious, "Nobody dares to convict you, but the police will come after me, and I can't escape responsibility! They'll drag me away and lock me up, and I don't want to spend the rest of my life sewing mailbags behind iron bars... Wait, do you even know what the police are?"

Long Mingze's brow knitted tightly, annoyed by my frantic output. He cast a silencing spell on me and said coldly, "Noisy!"

Unable to open my mouth, I could only gesture frantically with my hands.

His brow furrowed even deeper, and he said with extreme impatience, "Fine, I get it! I'll take care of the corpse, I won't let the police arrest you."

Seeing him flick his sleeve, making Wang Shuang's corpse vanish and restoring the messy room to its original state, I let out a slight sigh of relief.

Before leaving, Long Mingze leaned in close to me again, so close that the tip of his nose was almost touching my face.

His thin lips curved slightly into a wicked smile, "If you feel lonely in your boudoir again next time, you can come find me. I'll reluctantly satisfy you!"

I glared angrily as he vanished from my room.

Thinking of Wang Shuang's appearance when he died, I didn't dare stay in the bedroom any longer and ran back to the mourning hall to keep vigil for my grandmother.

***

The next morning, a heart-shattering scream woke everyone from their sleep.

'Ah...'

I had an ominous premonition, threw on a coat, and hurried outside.

From far away, I saw a crowd gathered around the large locust tree at the end of the village, a few of them even covering their mouths as if about to vomit.

The village chief, cigarette clamped in his mouth, had his brow furrowed so tightly it could crush a fly, looking utterly helpless.

I quietly squeezed my way in and saw a naked man lying beneath the tree. His corpse had been torn to shreds by wild beasts, not a single patch of good skin left on his entire body.

Internal organs and intestines had spilled out from his abdominal cavity and were frozen into ice, sticking to his skin. The manner of death was too gruesome to behold.

Had I not eaten practically nothing for the past two days, I probably would have run off to vomit as well.

Although that face had been clawed beyond recognition by sharp talons, I still recognized that it was none other than Wang Shuang!

Long Mingze had promised me he would take care of the body. Is this how he took care of it?

Uncle Ma, who lived at the end of the village, tucked his hands into his sleeves and sighed with emotion, "This morning, the village chief and I went to the back mountain to cut firewood together, and we found him in the potter's field. Who knows what wild beast chewed him up; he couldn't even be pieced together into a whole body!"

I remained unsettled for a long time, the hatred in my heart toward Long Mingze deepening another layer.

At that moment, Wang Shuang's parents pushed through the crowd. Upon seeing their son's miserable state, they nearly fainted.

Wang Shuang's mother threw herself onto the corpse, crying breathlessly, "Which damned beast harmed and killed my son?"

The villagers all kept their lips sealed.

Because Wang Shuang's family had moved away from Dragon-Guarding Village several years ago, strictly speaking, they were no longer considered people of our village.

Some even stepped forward to make cynical remarks, shrugging off responsibility.

"You lot used to stay in the village, didn't you know you shouldn't go up the mountain alone in early spring?"

This rule had been set by the village chief; accidents involving wild beasts hurting people had occurred twice before.

Our forest area was very large, and there were many wild beasts on the mountain, black bears, lynxes, wild boars, and even Siberian tigers.

Bears in particular had hibernated for several months, and the first thing they did upon leaving their dens was look for food, lunging at anything that moved lively.

Moreover, bears were the kind of animals that, once tainted with human blood, would regard humans as part of the food chain and would frequently come down the mountain to grab people in the future.

Fearing a repeat of such incidents, the village chief forbade villagers from going up the mountain alone in early spring.

Yet the injuries on Wang Shuang were not left by a black bear; bears did not eat dead meat.

Judging from those scattered and torn wounds, it was most likely a wild boar.

Hearing this, Wang Shuang's mother raised her head, swept her gaze from the crowd to me, and demanded harshly, "Lin Jianlu, make it clear to me! Last night my son ran out to look for you and didn't come back all night. How come he's dead this morning?"

Upon hearing that this matter had to do with me, the villagers quickly retreated ten meters away from me, all looking at me with terrified and fearful eyes.

Only Wang Shuang's mother, still clueless, stepped forward and grabbed my collar, shaking me while cursing vehemently, "You vixen! Back then, it was because of you that Wang Shuang couldn't even finish school, forcing our family to move to Guangdong!

Now that we've just come back, you've used your vixen tricks to latch onto him again. He made a fuss about going out to find you after dinner last night, and I couldn't stop him.

What on earth did you do to my son? Such a healthy, living man, how did he end up like this..."

chapters.title: Mulberry and Tussah Wood
chapters.content:
"Please watch your mouth. It was your son who wanted to rape me, I didn't pester him at all!" I wrenched myself free from her hands and said through clenched teeth.

Wang Shuang's mother wiped the tears from her face and firmly grabbed my arm, refusing to let me go.

"Everyone heard it, right? This vixen is the one who killed my son!"

The villagers looked at one another in dismay, none daring to speak.

Not understanding why, Wang Shuang's mother stamped her foot fiercely, pointed at the elders and villagers, and cursed, "Bah, you're all in this together! Village Chief, you're not going to do anything about this? Fine then, let's go to the police station and let the police handle it!"

The village chief hadn't wanted to show his face, but upon hearing Wang Shuang's mother threaten to blow the matter up, he had no choice but to step forward and smooth things over, "Sister Wang, don't get excited. This matter..."

"This matter can only be blamed on your son's daring lust, even daring to touch the Dragon King's woman!" Uncle Ma chimed in at the right moment.

His tone was exceptionally shrill, clearly indicating he was possessed by an immortal spirit.

The village chief frowned at him, "What do you mean by that?"

Uncle Ma hooked his fingers into an orchid mudra, covered his mouth and smiled, "Who else but that Wang Shuang, drooling over Lin Jianlu's body with his mind full of dirty garbage... When forced seduction failed, he enraged the Dragon King instead! Not having a complete body after death can also be considered the punishment inflicted upon him by the Dragon King!"

As Uncle Ma spoke, he turned and glanced at me.

That gaze instantly turned terrified, as if he saw something terrifying through me.

I turned back in confusion, but saw nothing.

Immediately afterward, Uncle Ma shivered, recovered his normal tone, waved his hand at me, and said, "I can't manage family matters like yours. Don't come looking for me anymore in the future!"

Before he finished speaking, he scurried back to his spirit hall in a flash.

The villagers were all in a fog, having no idea what had actually happened.

I guessed that most likely Dragon Mingze was playing tricks.

He had threatened Uncle Ma not to meddle in my affairs, so even though Uncle Ma had an immortal spirit on him, he didn't dare stick his head out again.

In the natural world, dragons could be called the ultimate terrestrial creatures.

Animals could ultimately only cultivate to become immortals, but dragons were ancient divine beasts with an innate aura of royalty, crushing everything.

Without that bloodline, an ordinary snake could ultimately only become a python or a jiao, but could never transform into a dragon.

From ancient times to the present, dragons had always been the masters of all things, and ordinary immortal spirits could not afford to offend them either.

After hearing Uncle Ma's words, Wang Shuang's parents looked a bit embarrassed.

Everyone in the village knew that their family had moved away back then precisely because Wang Shuang's pursuit of me failed and he was terrified at the Dragon King Temple.

Now that he had died without a whole corpse, it was because of me that he had offended the Dragon King!

"Dragon King, Dragon King... you're all barking on about my son offending the Dragon King! Today I'll smash this broken temple to see if that Dragon King is human or ghost!" Wang Shuang's father flew into a rage, picked up a hoe, and ran toward the Dragon King Temple.

The village chief wanted to stop them, but was frightened by the manic look of the couple, fearing that in their madness they might swing a hoe at him too.

The other villagers only dared stand outside the temple to watch the commotion, not daring to set foot inside the temple at all.

Wang Shuang's father's eyes were red with anger, and he swung his hoe straight at the brightly painted statue of the Dragon King.

An inexplicable bad premonition arose in my heart, and I was just about to open my mouth to stop him.

A sudden, earth-shattering thunderclap sounded in the sky, and countless streaks of black lightning overhead converged into a violent bolt of thunder, striking down toward the direction of the Dragon King Temple.

'Boom...'

Afterward, absolute silence descended.

Following a few daring villagers, I walked in on tiptoe.

The temple was in utter chaos, and the dust was thick enough to make one sneeze.

The town-dragon coffin was long gone, and the Dragon King statue had collapsed to the ground, landing squarely on top of Wang Shuang's parents.

The internal organs of Wang Shuang's parents had been crushed by the stone statue, and spitting blood, they had already breathed their last...

Someone was the first to shout out, "The Dragon King... the Dragon King has killed someone!"

Then, the surrounding villagers began to whisper among themselves in low voices.

"In broad daylight, how could this Dragon King still kill people? Could it be that what we've worshipped for so many years is actually an evil god?"

"It seems those legends are true. What's worshipped in this temple isn't any Dragon King, but that rampaging black jiao!"

"It's her, she's the one who let that evil jiao out!" Someone pointed at me and shouted sternly.

I was powerless to defend myself and stood there looking around blankly.

The villagers retreated from the Dragon King Temple one after another.

Even Aunt Wang stayed far away from me now, the look she cast my way mixed with fear, terror, and vigilance, as if treating me like a flood or a ferocious beast.

The only thing they didn't treat me as was a human.

"We're done for now. That evil jiao eats people! It killed Wang Shuang's family as soon as it came out; who knows if it'll eat young boys and girls next!"

I blame this Lin Jianlu. Why on earth did she have to let that evil jiao out? Is she trying to get us all killed?"

"Shut your trap a bit. If that evil jiao hears you, it'll come and eat you tonight!"

Those people whispered and discussed all at once, completely disregarding my presence, getting more and more outrageous.

The village chief furrowed his brow, unable to listen any longer, and shouted loudly, "Shut up, all of you. This has nothing to do with you anymore, go back to your rooms and stay inside!"

The village chief still held some prestige in everyone's hearts, and the crowd scattered like a tide, every household locking their doors and windows tightly, not daring to come out again.

"Xiaolu..." The village chief came up to me, but kept a distance of one meter away, not daring to get too close, and smiled apologetically.

"Don't take what everyone said to heart. They're just terrified by what's happened these past few days, they aren't targeting you on purpose."

I remained silent, my gaze somewhat unfocused.

The village chief hesitated for a moment and spoke cautiously, "We're all deeply saddened that something like this happened in your family. The police will naturally investigate Wang Shuang's matter clearly and clear your name.

However, you've seen it too; everyone has... a bit of prejudice against you right now. It's best if you don't show your face in front of everyone these days."

I gave a bitter smile and nodded, "I understand, Village Chief. Don't worry."

Having obtained my promise, the village chief hurried away as if fleeing.

I walked back desolately. The street was completely empty, and I had never felt the road from the entrance of the village to my house to be so long.

The resentment in my heart toward Dragon Mingze reached its peak, and even I began to doubt, was he truly that Dragon King who saved the world?

If grandmother were still here, I would surely ask her: were the stories passed down from ancient times written down wrong somewhere?

Why were Dragon Mingze's methods so cruel and despicable?

Treating human lives like ants, trampling and toying with them at will!

Yet, unfortunately, grandmother still lay peacefully before me, entirely devoid of life.

Suddenly, a faint halo gathered in the corner and slowly materialized into a human shape...

My pupils contracted, and I retreated defensively toward the bedside, "Dragon Mingze, how dare you still show your face!"

Long Mingze lazily rubbed the back of his neck and said idly, "Why wouldn't I dare?"

"You've caused the elders and villagers to treat me like an evil spirit. Now I've been forsaken by everyone, and even Aunt Wang is unwilling to see me. Are you satisfied?" The grievance and anger I had suppressed for days finally erupted, and I shouted at him.

chapters.title: Great Torrent Water
chapters.content:
Hearing this, a flash of smug delight crossed the depths of Long Mingze's eyes. "How can you blame me? You humans are naturally such creatures! Cowardly and fearful of the unknown, thinking only of destruction and expulsion. Non-kin of ours, their hearts must be different...

I made you see their true nature clearly. What is wrong with that?"

"Of course I know humans are selfish, cowardly, and greedy; I don't need you to remind me!" I retorted coldly. "Why are you showing off your racial superiority here? Relying on the fact that you're a dragon and slaughtering the weak at will, just how noble are you? Even if Wang Shuang was guilty, what crime did his parents commit?"

Long Mingze's expression shifted from arrogant to furious, the corners of his eyes flushed a faint red. "They smashed my temple and destroyed my divine statue. Shouldn't they die?"

"That was only after you killed Wang Shuang first; that's why they went to smash your temple. With all your supernatural powers, you could have just thought of a way to drive them out. Why did you have to kill them?"

I raised my chin, meeting his gaze without fear. "I actually think Wang Shuang's parents did the right thing. You are so cruel and vicious, you don't deserve to be the Dragon King of the Heilongjiang River at all!"

These words completely enraged Long Mingze. He walked toward me step by step, like a blood-soaked Asura crawling out of purgatory, a sinister smile blooming on his lips. "What did you just say? Say it again."

"I said you don't deserve people's offerings..."

Before I could finish, he grabbed me by the throat.

Just like he had done to Wang Shuang, he lifted me into the air.

My fragile windpipe emitted a dangerous, faint creak, and my legs kicked desperately toward him in mid-air, but his grip was like iron pliers, and my breath grew increasingly thin.

With the thought of perishing together, I tore the black jade from my chest and slashed it heavily across his neck. Sure enough, he let go.

"Cough, cough..." I slumped to the ground, gasping desperately.

Raising my eyes, I saw a five-centimeter-long scratch on Long Mingze's neck. Blood flowed down his neckline, staining his snow-white collar red.

When I slashed Wen Youcai, I hadn't used much force at all, yet his entire palm had been severed.

Yet when I slashed Long Mingze with the black jade, using all my strength, it only managed to carve a shallow bloody gash.

This thing really knows how to judge who it's dealing with...

Long Mingze looked with an incredulous expression at the piece of black jade in my palm, his face turning extremely ugly as he shook his head and said, "No, this is impossible! Long Mingyuan actually gave this thing to you? Has he gone mad..."

"What on earth is this thing? A protective talisman?" I asked.

Come to think of it, ever since the wedding night on the second day of the second lunar month, I hadn't seen Long Mingyuan once.

Judging by Long Mingze's implication, he seemed to have caused Long Mingyuan a lot of trouble, keeping him too busy to get away.

And Long Mingyuan had also indicated that he would not see me again in the future, so what on earth are he and I... considered to be?

Long Mingze did not answer. Seeing me clutching that piece of black jade tightly, holding it against my chest like a weapon, he sneered.

"Put that worthless piece of junk away, and stop making a fool of yourself! I said, I didn't want to kill you, otherwise, for your repeated provocations against me, I would have already reduced your bones to ashes!"

I pressed my lips together and remained silent, not lowering my guard.

Instead, Long Mingze calmed down, pacing leisurely around my room like he was taking a stroll in a courtyard. He walked over to Granny's bed and reached out as if to touch her.

"Don't touch my grandmother!" I spread my arms and blocked the front of Granny, my tone as stern as ice.

Long Mingze didn't care at all, lifting his eyelids to survey the room full of pure white mourning halls. "Are you... holding a funeral? Your grandmother isn't even dead yet; why are you in such a hurry to send her off!"

I was startled. "What did you say?"

"I said, your grandmother isn't dead." Long Mingze repeated impatiently.

"You mean my grandmother can still come back to life?" I pursued anxiously.

Long Mingze placed his hand above Granny's forehead, and a wisp of black light leaked from his palm, as if he were probing Granny's condition.

"Your grandmother is a shaman. She should have died a naturally occurring death after the deities vanished. I don't know what kind of thing took your grandmother's soul, turning her into a living corpse with no consciousness at all. If you can find her soul back, there might still be hope!"

"Really?" This was the only good news I had heard in days.

Before a smile could even form on my face, however, he poured another basin of cold water over me.

"But her physical body no longer has any signs of life. Soon, like a corpse, it will gradually rot and fester. You have less than half a month left."

I slumped again.

The clue previously given by the Nine-Tailed Fox Fairy had completely broken off once it reached the Wen family.

To find the person who snatched away Granny's soul within half a month was simply like looking for a needle in a haystack!

Long Mingze spoke up at just the right moment. "Considering you are my princess consort, let me point you down a bright path. The Greater Khingan Mountains are rich in wild ginseng, and among them is a thousand-year-old ginseng. Eating it can bring the dead back to life and flesh out bare bones...

If you go dig up that ginseng and feed it to your grandmother, it can at least buy you three to five months of time, keeping her flesh from rotting. That should be enough time for you to find her soul."

I felt as though I had caught a glimpse of a ray of hope.

The elderly in the village used to say that a thousand-year-old ginseng did exist in our forests, but no one had ever managed to catch it.

Ginseng from those days had already turned into a spirit, looking exactly like a little child in appearance, able to cry and make a fuss.

It would also tease people who went up the mountain to dig for ginseng, deliberately pointing them in the wrong direction and trapping them in the mountains.

We all called it the 'Ginseng Doll.'

At the same time, my guard went up, and I quietly scrutinized Long Mingze. "Would you be so kind?"

"You don't have to believe me, but your grandmother only has half a month left to live. Figure it out yourself!" He raised his eyebrows disdainfully.

I couldn't just watch Granny rot away day by day. Even if Long Mingze was lying, I had no other options left right now and could only take the risk.

After Long Mingze vanished, I rummaged through Granny's sewing kit and cut off a length of red string.

The elders said that after digging up ginseng, you must tie it up with a red string, otherwise it would transform into a human shape and run away.

I didn't know yet whether the rumors were reliable, but preparing it first definitely wouldn't hurt.

I shouldered my herb-gathering basket and walked toward the back mountain.

The snow in the mountains had not yet melted, and the steep mountain paths were still very difficult to walk. Fortunately, it wasn't dark yet, and wild beasts wouldn't roam about during the day.

As a result, it took me several hours just to reach the mountainside. I was exhausted and panting, picking up a branch to use as a walking stick as I leaned on it and continued deeper into the forest.

The further I walked, the more I felt that Long Mingze was lying to me.

Usually, people chose August or September to dig for ginseng. In summer, the weather is hot, all the snow melts into the soil, and the ginseng sprouts out of the ground, bearing cherry-red fruit. Ginseng diggers could use the fruit to locate the ginseng.

Right now, the road surface was covered with half a meter of deep snow; where on earth was I supposed to find ginseng!

The sky was gradually growing dark, and continuing deeper would probably be dangerous. I'd better go home first and think of another way.

Just as I planned to retrace my steps, a familiar, aged cry for help suddenly reached my ears.

"Is anyone there? Oh dear, help..."

***

chapters.title: Sand-Embedded Earth
chapters.content:
I followed the sound and saw an old man wearing a green military overcoat sitting under a tree root not far away, clutching his stomach and letting out painful wails.

The paper-doll-old-sister incident from last time had left me with a bit of caution. I raised my flashlight and shined it over, examining the person carefully from head to toe.

Making sure he wasn't made of paper, but a real human being with skin texture, I finally dared to step forward and ask.

"Mister, what's wrong?"

"Little girl, I went up the mountain to cut firewood and got lost." The old man dragged out a mournful tone, tears flickering in his turbid eyes. "Do you have anything to eat on you? My stomach is twisting in pain from hunger!"

Without hesitation, I took a flatbread from my pocket and handed it to him. "It's already cold, but please make do with a bite first."

The old man grabbed it quickly and began devouring it wolf-style, mumbling vaguely, "Little girl, you have such a kind heart!"

Having walked without a break for several hours, my physical strength was also near depletion. I leaned against a tree next to him to rest and asked casually, "Mister, which village are you from? Why haven't I seen you before?"

The old man acted as if he hadn't heard me and continued to gnaw blindly on that piece of flatbread.

Thinking this old man was mostly deaf, I shouted even louder, "Mister, which village are you from?"

Still, the old man didn't reply. Instead, a dry, hoarse voice came from behind me.

"Xiaolu, what are you shouting blindly about here?"

I turned my head and saw a middle-aged woman wearing a red short jacket, with a vegetable basket hanging from her elbow, walking in my direction.

I recognized this woman; she was Aunt Zhang from the neighboring village.

Her daughter had married into our village a couple of years ago, and Aunt Zhang often crossed the river to visit her.

"Aunt Zhang, you're going out just as the snow has finally stopped?" I greeted her politely.

Aunt Zhang said breathlessly, "Taking advantage of the snow stopping, I want to go to town to buy some good food for my daughter to nourish herself. She's just got with child; how can she possibly eat pickled cabbage and vermicelli stew every day!"

My heart felt a bit sour. Comparing Aunt Zhang's affection for her daughter with Fu Hongmei, who wished she could strangle me; they were both mothers, so why was the gap between them so huge!

"It's completely dark now, and the wild beasts will be coming out of their dens soon. Even if you're in a hurry, it wouldn't hurt to wait half a day, right? Why don't you come back to the village with me first, and we'll set off tomorrow morning." I kindly advised.

Hearing the eagle owls making a shrill *jiejie* sound above our heads, Aunt Zhang showed a look of fear and nodded.

I turned around, intending to take the lost old man down the mountain with us so we could look after each other.

As a result, the old man was no longer anywhere to be found under the tree...

Strange, I hadn't even heard footsteps.

That old man had been so hungry he couldn't even stand up just a moment ago; how did eating a piece of flatbread turn him into someone who could move like flying, disappearing in the blink of an eye?

Could that flatbread have been Popeye-brand spinach-stuffed flatbread!

"Aunt Zhang, did you see the old man who was just talking to me? Where did he go?" I asked.

Aunt Zhang's face, shriveled like accumulated ravines, showed a solemn look. "What old man? Just now I saw you standing there all by yourself, which is why I called out to you, wondering if this child was bewitched, shouting and yelling at a tree!"

I widened my eyes in disbelief. "Didn't you see an old man in a green military overcoat? He was sitting right under that tree, saying he was lost, and even asked me for a flatbread!"

As I spoke, I reached out to touch my pocket, my expression instantly turning bewildered.

Because I felt around in my pocket again and pulled out another flatbread, frozen stiff as a board...

I was completely certain that I had only packed one flatbread when I left home, and I had given it to that old man just now.

Yet now, how did another flatbread magically appear in my pocket?

Aunt Zhang looked at me with the gaze one would give a fool. "There's no old man anywhere. I only ever saw you by yourself!"

Now I was dazed too. Could that old man be...

"Huh?" Aunt Zhang frowned and fell into deep thought as well. "Now that you mention it, I seem to remember! There really is an old man in our village who wears a green military overcoat. But he died twenty-five years ago; you shouldn't have ever seen him!"

It would have been better if Aunt Zhang hadn't said that. Hearing her words, my already cold body turned thoroughly ice-choked.

And yet Aunt Zhang's floodgates of speech refused to stop!

"That old man went up the mountain to cut firewood in the dead of winter, but he ran into a blizzard, got trapped in the mountains, couldn't come back, and starved to death. The village's herb gatherer only found him when spring came. He was wearing that very same military overcoat, and his body was frozen into an ice sculpture..."

"Aunt... Aunt Zhang, stop talking!" My teeth chattered lightly as I pretended that what I had seen was merely an illusion.

"Alright, I won't talk anymore. Let's hurry home." Aunt Zhang replied readily, slinging her vegetable basket over her arm and taking the lead to walk in front of me.

I couldn't help but admire the elders in the village. They had grown up relying on gathering mountain goods for a living, and their physical stamina was top-notch.

That Aunt Zhang was over fifty years old, yet her steps were still robust and agile.

I was chasing behind her to the point of getting a stitch in my side, leaning against a tree branch and breathing heavily.

The moment I raised my head, I abruptly realized that we had actually walked into that potter's field graveyard on the back mountain...

The moonlight filtered through the overlapping tree branches, casting eerie shadows on the snow and making the scattered, broken tombstones look even more sinister.

A chilling, bone-piercing wind swept through the middle, letting out groans like wailing ghosts, as if unknown creatures were hiding in the dark and secretly watching me.

"Aunt Zhang, did we take the wrong turn? I remember the way back to the village doesn't pass through here, does it?" I shivered as I looked around us.

At that moment, I caught sight of a newly built grave not far away. There were still tattered funeral wreaths and paper money on the snow that hadn't been completely ruined, and judging by appearances, the burial couldn't have been more than three months ago.

Gaining courage, I shined my flashlight onto the marble tombstone. The black-and-white photo pasted on it revealed a face that completely exceeded my expectations!

The person in the photo was actually Aunt Zhang!

I suddenly recalled that before the final exams, Granny had mentioned in passing on the phone that Aunt Zhang from the neighboring village hadn't made it through the New Year and had passed away from illness around the winter solstice.

Since Aunt Zhang didn't have much contact with our family, I had forgotten all about it after hearing it.

Now, looking at the words on the tombstone once more, it made my hair stand on end.

Tomb of Loving Mother Zhang Yufen, Erected in Filial Piety by Daughter Li Menglian.

A small line of characters carved underneath gave the burial date, precisely three months ago...

Aunt Zhang, who had been standing in front of me, slowly turned her head. That wrinkled face turned as pale as frost in the moonlight, and two lines of bloody tears streamed from her eyes as she grinned at me.

"Xiaolu, didn't I just... bring you home?"

I was so frightened I couldn't even scream; I turned on my heel and ran back the way I came.

Aunt Zhang's sinister and shrill voice still called out behind me, "Xiaolu, don't run away! Come on home with Auntie!"

Who wants to go home with you? Your coffin couldn't possibly fit two people!
